## 1. Data Preparation

### 1.a Data preparation before the analysis

Full CSNT test data are extracted from GRID based on 'flags_form field, *which is the record against individual application*.

'timecompleted' variable is chosen as the criterion date selection. fielddata is selected to refer to Subject ID.

Two datasets were pulled from GRID, one for all the item, test level and diversity data. Second dataset contained vacancy information-grade and other diversity data.

Annual data is between 01 January to 31 December based on timecompleted.

File path is set to run from the desktop. Next, Data without 'timecompleted' are dropped so that incomplete test instances are not included in IRT analysis. This also decreases data sparsity.

```{r}
#| label: env-file-check
#| message: false
#| warning: false

cat("Working directory:", getwd(), "\n")

p1 <- path.expand("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_10_22_CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored.xlsx")
p2 <- path.expand("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_10_22_CSNT_All_Grade_Type.csv")

cat("Scored XLSX exists:", file.exists(p1), "| Size (MB):", round(file.info(p1)$size / 1e6, 2), "\n")
cat("Grade CSV exists:  ", file.exists(p2), "| Size (MB):", round(file.info(p2)$size / 1e6, 2), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: load-and-clean-datasets
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. READ RAW DATASETS WITHOUT OVERWRITING SOURCE FILES
raw_scored_path <- path.expand("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_10_22_CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored.xlsx")
raw_grade_path  <- path.expand("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_10_22_CSNT_All_Grade_Type.csv")

stopifnot(file.exists(raw_scored_path), file.exists(raw_grade_path))

CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored <- readxl::read_excel(raw_scored_path) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(timecompleted)

# Drop columns that are completely NA across all rows
all_na_cols <- vapply(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored, function(col) all(is.na(col)), logical(1))
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored[, !all_na_cols, drop = FALSE]

CSNT_All_Grade_Type <- utils::read.csv(raw_grade_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

cat(sprintf(
  "Scored rows: %d | Grade/Type rows: %d\n",
  nrow(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored), nrow(CSNT_All_Grade_Type)
))
```

(Added variables from the Otap_Vac table to get the grades and applicant types: Merge datasets based on fielddata). Data is merged here. This could add extra diversity data without test completions.

```{r}
# 1. Clean 'fielddata' in place as non-scientific whole-number strings
df1_clean <- CSNT_All_Grade_Type %>%
  mutate(fielddata = trimws(sprintf("%.0f", as.numeric(fielddata))))

df2_clean <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored %>%
  mutate(fielddata = trimws(sprintf("%.0f", as.numeric(fielddata))))

# 2. Join datasets directly on 'fielddata'
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored <- left_join(df1_clean, df2_clean, by = "fielddata")

# 3. Check matches using a column that exists ONLY in df2_clean (not df1_clean)
df2_only_cols <- setdiff(names(df2_clean), names(df1_clean))
col_from_df2 <- df2_only_cols[1]

match_count <- sum(!is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored[[col_from_df2]]))
cat("Number of matching rows:", match_count, "out of", nrow(df1_clean), "\n")
```

### 1.b. Creating annual dataset -2025

For the purpose of analysing annual dataset, test completions in year 2025 (based on 'timecompleted') were selected.

```{r}
temp<- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored 
temp$timecompleted<-as.numeric(substr(temp$timecompleted, 1,4))
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025<-filter(temp, timecompleted==2025)
```

### 1.b.1 Remove duplicate candidate instances based on 'timecompleted'

While all may be completed test instances there may be multiple instances of test takers. So, duplicates are dropped from the IRT analysis based on column 'timecompleted'. First date is kept.

```{r}
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%
arrange(timecompleted) %>%      # Sort dates in ascending order (earliest first)
distinct(fielddata, .keep_all = TRUE) # Keep first occurrence per ID, retain all other columns
sum(duplicated(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$fielddata))
```

### 1.b.5 Select Only active items to evaluate test performance.

Trial items are dropped from the data. Additionally, test items with no variance are dropped.

```{r}
# 1. READ METADATA & GET ACTIVE ITEM NAMES 
item_metadata <- read_excel("~/Documents/R Studio Work/CSNT_Item_Usage_2026_All.xlsx")

active_items_list <- item_metadata %>%
  filter(Type == "Active") %>%
  pull(ItemID)

# 2. SUBSET MASTER DATA & ENFORCE VARIANCE FILTERING
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
id_var <- "fielddata"

# Extract active item columns from 2025 master dataset
active_matrix_raw <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(any_of(active_items_list))

# Calculate p-values (item means) to find zero-variance items
item_p_values <- colMeans(active_matrix_raw, na.rm = TRUE)

# Filter criteria: Non-NaN AND 0 < p-value < 1 (removes zero-variance items)
valid_variance_cols <- !is.nan(item_p_values) & item_p_values > 0 & item_p_values < 1

# Subset item matrix to active + non-zero variance items only
clean_active_items2025 <- active_matrix_raw[, valid_variance_cols]

cat("Active items requested:", length(active_items_list), "\n")
cat("Active items retained (non-zero variance):", ncol(clean_active_items2025), "\n")
cat("Zero-variance active items dropped:", sum(!valid_variance_cols), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. FILTER OUT PARTICIPANTS WITH NO RESPONSES ON ACTIVE ITEMS

# Logical mask for participants with AT LEAST ONE response across active items
valid_rows_active <- rowSums(!is.na(clean_active_items2025)) > 0

# Extract pure matrix passed to mirt() (no IDs, no demographic cols)
mirt_active_matrix <- clean_active_items2025[valid_rows_active, ]

cat("Participants analyzed in mirt():", nrow(mirt_active_matrix), "\n")
```

### 1.b.6 Item acceptance limit

```{r}
#| label: item-sample-size-check
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. SET IRT THRESHOLD (200 = 1PL operational; 100 = 1PL pilot; 500 = 2PL)
min_n_1pl <- 200

# 2. IDENTIFY BINARY SCORED ITEM COLUMNS (0/1)
is_binary_item <- function(x) {
  vals <- stats::na.omit(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x))))
  length(vals) > 0 && all(vals %in% c(0, 1))
}

exclude_cols <- c("Theta_1PL", "Active_1PL_Theta", "NRTtheta", "NRT_Theta", "disability", "gender")
candidate_cols <- setdiff(colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025), exclude_cols)
item_cols <- candidate_cols[vapply(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[candidate_cols], is_binary_item, logical(1))]

# 3. COUNT VALID RESPONSES & FLAG LOW-N OR EXTREME P-VALUE ITEMS
item_n_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(item_cols, \(col) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[col]])))
  valid_n <- sum(!is.na(x))
  p_val   <- if (valid_n > 0) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Item            = col,
    Valid_Responses = valid_n,
    Missing_N       = sum(is.na(x)),
    P_Value         = p_val,
    Calibration_Status = dplyr::case_when(
      valid_n < 100        ~ "CRITICAL: Below 1PL Pilot Minimum (n < 100)",
      valid_n < min_n_1pl  ~ paste0("FLAG: Below 1PL Operational Threshold (n < ", min_n_1pl, ")"),
      p_val < 0.05 | p_val > 0.95 ~ "WARNING: Extreme Difficulty (p < 0.05 or > 0.95)",
      TRUE                 ~ "OK (Sufficient for 1PL)"
    )
  )
}) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Valid_Responses)

# 4. SUMMARY COUNTS & DISPLAY FLAGGED ITEMS
flagged_items <- item_n_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_starts(Calibration_Status, "OK"))

cat(sprintf(
  "Total items checked: %d | Ready for 1PL (n >= %d): %d | Flagged: %d\n",
  nrow(item_n_summary),
  min_n_1pl,
  sum(stringr::str_starts(item_n_summary$Calibration_Status, "OK")),
  nrow(flagged_items)
))

knitr::kable(flagged_items)
```

### 1.c Average Item Usage

```{r}
#| label: fig-total-item-usage
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of Total Item Usage (2025) per Person"
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Step 1: Count 0s, 1s, and total item usage per person
person_usage <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%           # Replace 'your_data' with your dataframe name
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("NR") & !starts_with("NRT"),
    names_to = "item",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  group_by(fielddata) %>%
  summarise(
    count_0     = sum(response == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_1     = sum(response == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_usage = count_0 + count_1,
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

# Preview the counts
head(person_usage)

# Step 2: Plot histogram of total item usage with count labels on top of each bar
ggplot(person_usage, aes(x = total_usage)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1,                       # Adjust binwidth if total_usage spans a wide range (e.g., 5 or 10)
    fill = "#2b5c8f",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  stat_bin(
    binwidth = 1,                       # Must match geom_histogram's binwidth
    geom = "text",
    aes(label = ifelse(after_stat(count) > 0, after_stat(count), "")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = mean(total_usage, na.rm = TRUE)),
    color = "#d9534f", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Total Item Usage per Person",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Mean Total Usage = ", round(mean(person_usage$total_usage, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      " items (n = ", nrow(person_usage), " persons)"
    ),
    x = "Total Item Usage (Count of 0s + Count of 1s)",
    y = "Number of Persons"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

Stopping rule for 0.5 SE does never activate at 10 item exposure implying items do not meet the stopping criteria. There are even cases where candidates have to solve the maximum 20 questions

## 2. RASCH Analysis

For the purpose of IRT analysis, Rasch, 1PL and 2PL methods were tested to compare model performances.

Rasch analysis was carried out with active items only.

```{r}
#| label: rasch-analysis-calibration
#| message: false
#| warning: false

min_n_rasch  <- 200
item_valid_n <- colSums(!is.na(mirt_active_matrix))
item_p_val   <- colMeans(mirt_active_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_items  <- names(item_valid_n)[item_valid_n >= min_n_rasch & !is.na(item_p_val) & item_p_val > 0 & item_p_val < 1]

stopifnot(length(valid_items) >= 2)

cal_mat_rasch <- mirt_active_matrix[, valid_items, drop = FALSE]

fit_rasch <- mirt::mirt(
  cal_mat_rasch,
  model = 1, itemtype = "Rasch", SE = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)

coef_list <- mirt::coef(fit_rasch, IRTpars = TRUE, printSE = TRUE)
fit_stats <- suppressWarnings(mirt::itemfit(fit_rasch, fit_stats = c("infit", "X2")))

cal_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Item         = valid_items,
  Difficulty_b = round(vapply(valid_items, function(i) as.numeric(coef_list[[i]][1, "b"]), numeric(1)), 3),
  SE_b         = round(vapply(valid_items, function(i) {
    if ("SE" %in% rownames(coef_list[[i]])) as.numeric(coef_list[[i]]["SE", "b"]) else NA_real_
  }, numeric(1)), 3),
  Infit_MSQ    = round(as.numeric(fit_stats$infit), 3),
  Z_Infit      = round(replace(as.numeric(fit_stats$z.infit), is.nan(fit_stats$z.infit), NA_real_), 3),
  Outfit_MSQ   = round(as.numeric(fit_stats$outfit), 3),
  Z_Outfit     = round(replace(as.numeric(fit_stats$z.outfit), is.nan(fit_stats$z.outfit), NA_real_), 3),
  X2_p_value   = round(as.numeric(fit_stats$p.X2), 4)
)

msq_flag <- ((pmin(fit_stats$infit, fit_stats$outfit, na.rm = TRUE) < 0.5) |
             (pmax(fit_stats$infit, fit_stats$outfit, na.rm = TRUE) > 1.5))

cat(
  "Calibrated:", length(valid_items),
  "; Excluded:", ncol(mirt_active_matrix) - length(valid_items),
  "; Converged:", mirt::extract.mirt(fit_rasch, "converged"),
  "; MSQ Misfit:", sum(msq_flag, na.rm = TRUE),
  "; X2 Misfit:", sum(fit_stats$p.X2 < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n"
)

rasch_item_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Item    = colnames(mirt_active_matrix),
  Valid_N = as.integer(item_valid_n),
  Status  = dplyr::case_when(
    Item %in% valid_items      ~ "Calibrated",
    item_valid_n < min_n_rasch ~ paste0("Insufficient Data (n < ", min_n_rasch, ")"),
    TRUE                       ~ "Excluded (Zero Variance: p = 0 or 1)"
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cal_df, by = "Item")

knitr::kable(head(rasch_item_summary, 15))
```

### 2.a. Person Theta scores 2025

```{r}
#| label: rasch-person-scores
#| message: false
#| warning: false

rasch_person_scores <- mirt::fscores(fit_rasch, method = "EAP", full.scores = TRUE, full.scores.SE = TRUE)

id_var <- "fielddata"
stopifnot(id_var %in% names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))

# Align IDs directly with the rows of mirt_active_matrix / fit_rasch
if (nrow(mirt_active_matrix) == nrow(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  ids_rasch <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[id_var]]
} else {
  base_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(clean_active_items2025)) > 0
  ids_rasch <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[id_var]][base_rows]
}

stopifnot(length(ids_rasch) == nrow(rasch_person_scores))

has_cal_resp <- rowSums(!is.na(cal_mat_rasch)) > 0

rasch_theta_df <- tibble::tibble(
  !!id_var    := ids_rasch,
  Rasch_Theta  = ifelse(has_cal_resp, as.numeric(rasch_person_scores[, "F1"]), NA_real_),
  Rasch_SE     = ifelse(has_cal_resp, as.numeric(rasch_person_scores[, "SE_F1"]), NA_real_)
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[id_var]])) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data[[id_var]], .keep_all = TRUE)

CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Rasch_Theta", "Rasch_SE"))) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(rasch_theta_df, by = id_var, na_matches = "never")

cat(sprintf(
  "Scored & matched %d examinees (across %d calibrated items) to %d master rows.\n",
  sum(!is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Rasch_Theta)),
  length(valid_items),
  nrow(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)
))
```

Re-Check for item variance (6rows nonmatching due to NAs)

```{r}
#| label: rasch-unmatched-check
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (!exists("id_var")) id_var <- "fielddata"
stopifnot(id_var %in% names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025), "Rasch_Theta" %in% names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))

unmatched_idx <- which(
  is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Rasch_Theta) |
  is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[id_var]])
)

cat("Unmatched / unscored rows:", length(unmatched_idx), "\n")

if (length(unmatched_idx) > 0) {
  act_cols <- intersect(colnames(mirt_active_matrix), names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))
  cal_cols <- intersect(valid_items, act_cols)

  all_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(
    CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[unmatched_idx, act_cols, drop = FALSE],
    function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  ))
  cal_mat  <- all_mat[, cal_cols, drop = FALSE]
  cal_n    <- rowSums(!is.na(cal_mat))
  cal_mean <- rowMeans(cal_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  centered <- sweep(cal_mat, 1, cal_mean, "-")

  unmatched_summary <- tibble::tibble(
    Row          = unmatched_idx,
    ID           = as.character(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[id_var]][unmatched_idx]),
    Active_N     = rowSums(!is.na(all_mat)),
    Calibrated_N = cal_n,
    Cal_Variance = ifelse(cal_n > 1, round(rowSums(centered^2, na.rm = TRUE) / (cal_n - 1), 3), NA_real_),
    Reason       = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(ID)         ~ "Missing ID",
      Active_N == 0     ~ "No active item responses",
      Calibrated_N == 0 ~ "Answered excluded (low-N) items only",
      TRUE              ~ "Duplicate / unmatched ID"
    )
  )

  reason_counts <- unmatched_summary %>%
    dplyr::count(Reason, name = "Rows")

  print(knitr::kable(reason_counts, caption = "Summary of Unmatched / Unscored Rows"))
  print(knitr::kable(utils::head(unmatched_summary, 20), caption = "First 20 Unmatched / Unscored Rows"))
}
```

### 2.b. Person-Item Map (Wright Map) for fit_rasch

```{r}
#| label: rasch-wright-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

stopifnot(exists("cal_df"), "Difficulty_b" %in% names(cal_df), "Item" %in% names(cal_df))

cal_only <- dplyr::filter(cal_df, !is.na(Difficulty_b), !is.na(Item))
rasch_b  <- as.numeric(cal_only$Difficulty_b)

theta_vec <- if (exists("rasch_theta_df") && "Rasch_Theta" %in% names(rasch_theta_df)) {
  rasch_theta_df$Rasch_Theta
} else if (exists("CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025") && "Rasch_Theta" %in% names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Rasch_Theta
} else {
  numeric(0)
}

valid_thetas <- as.numeric(stats::na.omit(theta_vec))
stopifnot(length(rasch_b) > 0, length(valid_thetas) > 0)

# Build combined dataset sharing one vertical Logit scale
panel_levels <- c(
  sprintf("Person Ability (N = %s)", format(length(valid_thetas), big.mark = ",")),
  sprintf("Item Difficulty (K = %d)", length(rasch_b))
)

wright_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Logit = valid_thetas, Panel = panel_levels[1]),
  tibble::tibble(Logit = rasch_b,      Panel = panel_levels[2])
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Panel = factor(Panel, levels = panel_levels))

means_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Panel = factor(panel_levels, levels = panel_levels),
  Mean  = c(mean(valid_thetas), mean(rasch_b)),
  Label = sprintf("Mean = %.2f", c(mean(valid_thetas), mean(rasch_b)))
)

ggplot2::ggplot(wright_df, ggplot2::aes(y = Logit)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(
    ggplot2::aes(x = ggplot2::after_stat(density), fill = Panel),
    bins = 35, alpha = 0.75, color = "white", linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    data = means_df,
    ggplot2::aes(yintercept = Mean),
    linetype = "dashed", color = "#1a252f", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = means_df,
    ggplot2::aes(x = Inf, y = Mean, label = Label),
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#1a252f"
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Panel, scales = "free_x") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2c7fb8", "#d95f02")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "Wright Map: Person Ability vs. Item Difficulty (2025)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Targeting gap (Mean Person - Mean Item): %.2f logits",
      mean(valid_thetas) - mean(rasch_b)
    ),
    x = "Density",
    y = "Logit Scale (Theta / Difficulty b)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    strip.text       = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    plot.title       = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

The above graph shows the mismatch between candidate abilities and item difficulties in the item bank.

### 2.c. Export Report to Excel

```{r}

#| label: Export_rasch-Excel
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# 1. PREPARE PARTICIPANT DATASET FOR EXPORT (Consistent Rasch_Theta / Rasch_SE names)}
rasch_participant_export <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::any_of(c(id_var, "timecompleted", "year_completed", "Rasch_Theta", "Rasch_SE"))
  )

# 2. CREATE WORKBOOK & ADD SHEETS
```

## 3. 1PL Analysis

### 3.a IRT Model 3.b. Getting Fit Statistics

**`mirt` standard error estimation fails on large datasets (320 items)** or fails to converge on the Information matrix computation, causing `pars_1pl_list$se` to silently return `NULL` (length 0).

When `mirt` encounters numerical instability during SE computation, it drops the standard errors entirely while keeping the parameter estimates.

**Failsafe Length Matching:** `se_a_vec` and `se_b_vec` are guaranteed to have exactly **320 elements** regardless of whether `mirt` successfully computed standard errors or returned `NULL`.

```{r}
#| label: 1pl-calibration
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. FILTER ACTIVE ITEMS BY MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE & VARIANCE
min_n_1pl       <- 200
item_valid_n    <- colSums(!is.na(mirt_active_matrix))
item_p_val      <- colMeans(mirt_active_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_items_1pl <- names(item_valid_n)[item_valid_n >= min_n_1pl & item_p_val > 0 & item_p_val < 1]

fit_1pl <- mirt::mirt(
  data     = mirt_active_matrix[, valid_items_1pl, drop = FALSE],
  model    = 1,
  itemtype = "1PL",
  SE       = TRUE,
  verbose  = FALSE
)

cat(
  "1PL Calibrated:", length(valid_items_1pl),
  "| Excluded:", ncol(mirt_active_matrix) - length(valid_items_1pl),
  "| Converged:", mirt::extract.mirt(fit_1pl, "converged"), "\n"
)

# 2. EXTRACT ITEM PARAMETERS, SEs & FIT STATS IN ONE PASS
coef_se_1pl  <- mirt::coef(fit_1pl, IRTpars = TRUE, printSE = TRUE)
item_fit_1pl <- suppressWarnings(mirt::itemfit(fit_1pl, fit_stats = "infit"))

get_par <- function(items, row_nm, col_nm) {
  vapply(items, function(itm) {
    mat <- coef_se_1pl[[itm]]
    if (!is.null(mat) && row_nm %in% rownames(mat) && col_nm %in% colnames(mat)) {
      as.numeric(mat[row_nm, col_nm])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  }, numeric(1))
}

cal_1pl_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Item         = valid_items_1pl,
  Slope_a      = round(get_par(valid_items_1pl, "par", "a"), 3),
  SE_a         = round(get_par(valid_items_1pl, "SE",  "a"), 3),
  Difficulty_b = round(get_par(valid_items_1pl, "par", "b"), 3),
  SE_b         = round(get_par(valid_items_1pl, "SE",  "b"), 3),
  Infit_MSQ    = round(as.numeric(item_fit_1pl$infit), 3),
  Outfit_MSQ   = round(as.numeric(item_fit_1pl$outfit), 3)
)

# 3. BUILD MASTER 1PL ITEM SUMMARY TABLE (INCLUDING EXCLUDED ITEMS)
summary_1pl <- tibble::tibble(
  Item    = colnames(mirt_active_matrix),
  Valid_N = as.integer(item_valid_n),
  Status  = dplyr::case_when(
    Item %in% valid_items_1pl ~ "Calibrated",
    item_valid_n < min_n_1pl  ~ paste0("Insufficient Data (n < ", min_n_1pl, ")"),
    TRUE                      ~ "Excluded (Zero Variance: p = 0 or 1)"
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cal_1pl_df, by = "Item")

knitr::kable(head(summary_1pl, 15))

# 4. OVERALL DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY (CALIBRATED ITEMS ONLY)
summary_stats_1pl <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Total Active Items", "Calibrated Items", "Excluded Items",
    "Common Slope (a)", "Mean Difficulty (b)", "SD Difficulty",
    "Min Difficulty", "Max Difficulty", "Median Difficulty"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(summary_1pl),
    nrow(cal_1pl_df),
    nrow(summary_1pl) - nrow(cal_1pl_df),
    round(mean(cal_1pl_df$Slope_a, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(mean(cal_1pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(stats::sd(cal_1pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(min(cal_1pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(max(cal_1pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(stats::median(cal_1pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
  )
)

knitr::kable(summary_stats_1pl, caption = "1PL Item Difficulty Summary Statistics")
```

### 3.b Extracting Person ability and SEs

```{r}

#| label: 1pl-person-scores
#| message: false
#| warning: false

fscores_1pl <- mirt::fscores(fit_1pl, method = "EAP", full.scores = TRUE, full.scores.SE = TRUE)

id_var      <- "fielddata"
scored_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[, colnames(mirt_active_matrix), drop = FALSE])) > 0
has_cal_1pl <- rowSums(!is.na(mirt_active_matrix[, valid_items_1pl, drop = FALSE])) > 0

stopifnot(id_var %in% names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025), sum(scored_rows) == nrow(fscores_1pl))

theta_1pl_df <- tibble::tibble(
  !!id_var := CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[id_var]][scored_rows],
  Theta_1PL = ifelse(has_cal_1pl, as.numeric(fscores_1pl[, "F1"]), NA_real_),
  SE_1PL    = ifelse(has_cal_1pl, as.numeric(fscores_1pl[, "SE_F1"]), NA_real_)
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[id_var]])) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data[[id_var]], .keep_all = TRUE)

CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Theta_1PL", "SE_1PL"))) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(theta_1pl_df, by = id_var, na_matches = "never")

cat("Merged", sum(!is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL)), "calibrated 1PL scores.\n")
```

### 3.c 1PL Diagnostic Plots & Targeting Alignment (ICC + Person Density)

```{r}

#| label: 1pl-diagnostics-alignment
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# 1. TEST-LEVEL INFORMATION & CONDITIONAL SE (Essential CAT diagnostic)
plot(fit_1pl, type = "infoSE", main = "1PL Test Information & Conditional SE")

# 2. TARGETING ALIGNMENT PLOT (Uses filtered cal_1pl_df & valid Theta_1PL)
a_common     <- cal_1pl_df$Slope_a[1]
valid_thetas <- tibble::tibble(theta = stats::na.omit(theta_1pl_df$Theta_1PL))

icc_data_1pl <- tidyr::expand_grid(Item = cal_1pl_df$Item, theta = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 200)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cal_1pl_df[, c("Item", "Difficulty_b")], by = "Item") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(prob = stats::plogis(a_common * (theta - Difficulty_b)))

clean_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_icc <- ggplot(icc_data_1pl, aes(theta, prob, group = Item)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.45, color = "#2b5c8f", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-4, 4), breaks = -4:4) +
  labs(
    title    = "1PL Targeting Alignment: Calibrated Item Curves vs. Person Ability",
    subtitle = sprintf("Items = %d | Common slope a = %.3f | Dashed line = P(0.5) difficulty threshold", nrow(cal_1pl_df), a_common),
    x = NULL, y = "P(Theta)"
  ) +
  clean_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

p_dens <- ggplot(valid_thetas, aes(theta)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#e07a5f", color = "#c45d42", alpha = 0.6, adjust = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(valid_thetas$theta), color = "#8b2610", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-4, 4), breaks = -4:4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Latent Trait Ability (1PL Theta)", y = "Density") +
  clean_theme

p_icc / p_dens + plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1))
```

## 4. 2PL Analysis

### 4.a. IRT 2PL Model

First steps. Items with less than 500 responses are dropeed as per guidance.

```{r}
#| label: 2pl-calibration
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. FILTER ACTIVE ITEMS BY 2PL SAMPLE SIZE THRESHOLD & NON-ZERO VARIANCE
min_n_2pl       <- 500  # Operational 2PL minimum (use 250-300 for pilot/pretest items)
id_var          <- "fielddata"
item_valid_n    <- colSums(!is.na(mirt_active_matrix))
item_vars       <- apply(mirt_active_matrix, 2, stats::var, na.rm = TRUE)

valid_items_2pl <- names(item_valid_n)[
  item_valid_n >= min_n_2pl & !is.na(item_vars) & item_vars > 0
]

if (length(valid_items_2pl) < 2) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "Only %d item(s) met min_n_2pl = %d. Consider lowering min_n_2pl to 250 for pilot 2PL analysis.",
    length(valid_items_2pl), min_n_2pl
  ))
}

# Subset columns, then drop examinees who have 0 responses across retained 2PL items
mirt_2pl_sub    <- mirt_active_matrix[, valid_items_2pl, drop = FALSE]
keep_rows_2pl   <- rowSums(!is.na(mirt_2pl_sub)) > 0
mirt_2pl_matrix <- mirt_2pl_sub[keep_rows_2pl, , drop = FALSE]

cat(sprintf(
  "2PL Calibrated Items: %d of %d | Excluded: %d | Respondents Retained: %d\n",
  ncol(mirt_2pl_matrix), ncol(mirt_active_matrix),
  ncol(mirt_active_matrix) - ncol(mirt_2pl_matrix), nrow(mirt_2pl_matrix)
))

# 2. FIT 2PL MODEL (SE = FALSE kept for speed/stability on sparse CAT data)
fit_2pl <- mirt::mirt(
  data      = mirt_2pl_matrix,
  model     = 1,
  itemtype  = "2PL",
  SE        = FALSE,
  quadpts   = 21,
  TOL       = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000),
  verbose   = FALSE
)

cat("2PL Model Converged:", mirt::extract.mirt(fit_2pl, "converged"), "\n")

# 3. EXTRACT PARAMETERS & Zh ITEM FIT SAFELY
pars_2pl <- mirt::coef(fit_2pl, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

item_fit_2pl <- tryCatch(
  suppressWarnings(mirt::itemfit(fit_2pl, fit_stats = "Zh", na.rm = TRUE)),
  error = function(e) {
    warning("Zh item fit bypassed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

zh_vec <- if (!is.null(item_fit_2pl) && "Zh" %in% colnames(item_fit_2pl)) {
  round(as.numeric(item_fit_2pl$Zh), 3)
} else {
  rep(NA_real_, nrow(pars_2pl))
}

cal_2pl_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Item         = rownames(pars_2pl),
  Slope_a      = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "a"]), 3),
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "b"]), 3),
  Zh_Fit       = zh_vec
)

# 4. BUILD MASTER 2PL ITEM SUMMARY TABLE (INCLUDING EXCLUDED ITEMS)
summary_2pl <- tibble::tibble(
  Item    = colnames(mirt_active_matrix),
  Valid_N = as.integer(item_valid_n),
  Status  = dplyr::case_when(
    Item %in% valid_items_2pl ~ "Calibrated",
    item_valid_n < min_n_2pl  ~ paste0("Insufficient Data (n < ", min_n_2pl, ")"),
    TRUE                      ~ "Excluded (Zero Variance: p = 0 or 1)"
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cal_2pl_df, by = "Item")

knitr::kable(head(summary_2pl, 15))

# 5. OVERALL DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY (CALIBRATED 2PL ITEMS ONLY)
summary_stats_2pl <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Total Active Items", "Calibrated 2PL Items", "Excluded Items",
    "Mean Slope (a)", "SD Slope (a)", "Min Slope (a)", "Max Slope (a)",
    "Mean Difficulty (b)", "SD Difficulty (b)", "Min Difficulty (b)",
    "Max Difficulty (b)", "Median Difficulty (b)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(summary_2pl),
    nrow(cal_2pl_df),
    nrow(summary_2pl) - nrow(cal_2pl_df),
    round(mean(cal_2pl_df$Slope_a, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(stats::sd(cal_2pl_df$Slope_a, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(min(cal_2pl_df$Slope_a, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(max(cal_2pl_df$Slope_a, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(mean(cal_2pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(stats::sd(cal_2pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(min(cal_2pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(max(cal_2pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(stats::median(cal_2pl_df$Difficulty_b, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
  )
)

knitr::kable(summary_stats_2pl, caption = "2PL Item Parameter Summary Statistics")
```

```{r}
# 2. ALIGN IDS WITH RETAINED 2PL MATRIX ROWS
```

### Item Parameter Drift

This compares the current item difficulties to the new 1PL item difficulties.

```{r}
#| label: item_parameter_drift_graph
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# 1. LOAD 2021 ITEM PARAMETERS FROM EXCEL
df_2021_params <- read_excel("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_CSNT_ItemParameter2021_Usage2026.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet1") %>%
  mutate(Item_id = str_trim(as.character(Item_id))) %>%
  select(Item_id, Type, ItemStatus_Old, Total_Usage = Total, Difficulty_2021 = Item_Difficulty)

# 2. CLEAN & MERGE WITH NEW 1PL PARAMETERS (`summary_1pl`)
df_param_comp <- summary_1pl %>%
  mutate(Item = str_trim(as.character(Item))) %>%
  inner_join(df_2021_params, by = c("Item" = "Item_id")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Difficulty_2021), !is.na(Difficulty_b)) %>%
  mutate(
    Diff_Shift = Difficulty_b - Difficulty_2021,
    Abs_Shift  = abs(Diff_Shift),
    Drift_Flag = ifelse(Abs_Shift >= 0.30, "Large Drift (|Δb| ≥ 0.30)", "Stable (|Δb| < 0.30)")
  )

cat("Matched items with both 2021 and 2026 1PL parameters:", nrow(df_param_comp), "\n")
cat("Pearson correlation (r):", round(cor(df_param_comp$Difficulty_2021, df_param_comp$Difficulty_b), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean Signed Shift (New - Old):", round(mean(df_param_comp$Diff_Shift), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean Absolute Shift (MAD):", round(mean(df_param_comp$Abs_Shift), 4), "\n\n")

# ==============================================================================
# CHART 1: DUMBBELL PLOT SHOWING DISTANCE BETWEEN 2021 & NEW 1PL DIFFICULTY
# (Displays top 40 items with largest parameter shift; remove slice_max() to plot all)
# ==============================================================================
plot_data_dumbbell <- df_param_comp %>%
  slice_max(order_by = Abs_Shift, n = 40) %>%
  mutate(Item = reorder(Item, Diff_Shift))

p_dumbbell <- ggplot(plot_data_dumbbell, aes(y = Item)) +
  # Connecting line representing the distance (parameter drift)
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = Difficulty_2021, xend = Difficulty_b, yend = Item, color = Drift_Flag),
    linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  # 2021 Old Parameter Point
  geom_point(aes(x = Difficulty_2021, shape = "2021 Parameter (Old)"), color = "#4A6FE3", size = 2.8) +
  # 2026 New 1PL Parameter Point
  geom_point(aes(x = Difficulty_b, shape = "New 1PL Parameter"), color = "#D33F6A", size = 2.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Parameter Stability",
    values = c("Large Drift (|Δb| ≥ 0.30)" = "#D33F6A", "Stable (|Δb| < 0.30)" = "#7F8C8D")
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Calibration",
    values = c("2021 Parameter (Old)" = 16, "New 1PL Parameter" = 17)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Item Parameter Drift: 2021 Difficulty vs. New 1PL Difficulty (Top 40 Shifts)",
    subtitle = "Horizontal line length indicates exact distance (Δb = New 1PL − 2021)",
    x        = "Item Difficulty (b)",
    y        = "Item ID"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5)
  )

print(p_dumbbell)

# ==============================================================================
# CHART 2: FULL-BANK SCATTER PLOT WITH IDENTITY LINE (ALL MATCHED ITEMS)
 
# CHART 2: FULL-BANK SCATTER PLOT WITH IDENTITY LINE (No ggrepel required)
p_scatter <- ggplot(df_param_comp, aes(x = Difficulty_2021, y = Difficulty_b, color = Drift_Flag)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = df_param_comp %>% slice_max(Abs_Shift, n = 12),
    aes(label = Item),
    vjust = -0.7, size = 3, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Stability Threshold",
    values = c("Large Drift (|Δb| ≥ 0.30)" = "#D33F6A", "Stable (|Δb| < 0.30)" = "#2C7BB6")
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Full Item Bank Calibration Check: 2021 vs. New 1PL Difficulty",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = exact equivalence (y = x); vertical distance = parameter shift (Δb)",
    x        = "2021 Item Difficulty (Item_Difficulty)",
    y        = "New 1PL Item Difficulty (Difficulty_b)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_scatter)
```

## PHASE TWO

`type = 'LD'` produces local dependence metrics designed specifically for large item sets without triggering integer overflow:

### Unidimensionality Comparison ——————-

Unidimensionality Test. fit all three models under a single-factor structure and evaluate their **Global Fit Indices (**$M_2$, RMSEA, CFI, TLI), **Model Comparison Statistics (AIC, BIC, LRT)**, and **Local Independence (**$Q_3$).

Using `auto.prior = TRUE` handles this internally without needing manual parameter numbers.

When a 2PL Item Response Theory (IRT) model fails to converge—especially in large item sets or when dealing with sparse response patterns—it is almost always caused by **extreme parameter estimates** (slopes $a \to \infty$ or $a \le 0$) or **high correlation between items(AI)**.

```{r}
#| label: unidimensionality-comparison
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Set seed for reproducible sampling & scoring
set.seed(42)

# Define key identifier variable explicitly
id_var <- "fielddata"

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: CLEAN MATRIX PREPARATION (ZERO-VARIANCE REMOVAL)
item_vars    <- apply(mirt_active_matrix, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
clean_matrix <- mirt_active_matrix[, item_vars > 0 & !is.na(item_vars)]

cat("------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Original Items:", ncol(mirt_active_matrix), "\n")
cat("Clean Items (Variance > 0):", ncol(clean_matrix), "\n")
cat("Candidates in Matrix (N):", nrow(clean_matrix), "\n")
cat("Master Dataset Rows:", nrow(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025), "\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: FULL-MODEL ESTIMATION (RASCH, 1PL, 2PL)
cat("Fitting 1PL Model...\n")
fit_1pl <- mirt(
  clean_matrix, 
  model = 1, 
  itemtype = '1PL', 
  SE = FALSE, 
  quadpts = 21, 
  TOL = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), 
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("Fitting 2PL Model...\n")
fit_2pl <- mirt(
  clean_matrix, 
  model = 1, 
  itemtype = '2PL', 
  auto.prior = TRUE, 
  SE = FALSE, 
  quadpts = 21, 
  TOL = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), 
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("1PL Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_1pl, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("2PL Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_2pl, 'converged'), "\n\n")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: MEMORY-SAFE GLOBAL FIT INDICES (M2 VIA QMC WITH SAFE FALLBACK)
cat("Computing M2 Fit Indices on full models using QMC integration...\n")

# Safely compute M2 for 1PL
m2_1pl <- tryCatch({
  M2(fit_1pl, na.rm = TRUE, M2.a = TRUE, QMC = TRUE, quadpts = 15)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("1PL M2 calculation bypassed due to matrix size/vector limit: ", e$message)
  return(NULL)
})

# Safely compute M2 for 2PL
m2_2pl <- tryCatch({
  M2(fit_2pl, na.rm = TRUE, M2.a = TRUE, QMC = TRUE, quadpts = 15)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("2PL M2 calculation bypassed due to matrix size/vector limit: ", e$message)
  return(NULL)
})

# Extract basic model metrics guaranteed to exist
fit_1pl_loglik <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl, 'logLik')
fit_2pl_loglik <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl, 'logLik')

fit_1pl_aic    <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl, 'AIC')
fit_2pl_aic    <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl, 'AIC')

fit_1pl_bic    <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl, 'BIC')
fit_2pl_bic    <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl, 'BIC')

# Build summary table with conditional M2 fields
unidim_fit_summary <- data.frame(
  Model  = c("1PL", "2PL"),
  logLik = round(c(fit_1pl_loglik, fit_2pl_loglik), 2),
  AIC    = round(c(fit_1pl_aic, fit_2pl_aic), 2),
  BIC    = round(c(fit_1pl_bic, fit_2pl_bic), 2),
  M2     = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$M2, 2) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$M2, 2) else NA),
  df     = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) m2_1pl$df else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) m2_2pl$df else NA),
  RMSEA  = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$RMSEA, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$RMSEA, 3) else NA),
  CFI    = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$CFI, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$CFI, 3) else NA),
  TLI    = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$TLI, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$TLI, 3) else NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("\n=== UNIDIMENSIONAL GLOBAL FIT INDICES ===\n")
print(unidim_fit_summary) 

# ============================================================
# STEP 4: DIRECT MODEL COMPARISON (ANOVA / LIKELIHOOD RATIO TEST)
model_comp_anova <- anova(fit_1pl, fit_2pl)
model_comp_df    <- as.data.frame(model_comp_anova)

cat("\n=== MODEL COMPARISON (ANOVA / AIC / BIC) ===\n")
print(model_comp_df)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 5: MANUAL Q3 LOCAL INDEPENDENCE RESIDUAL CHECK
cat("\nComputing Yen's Q3 Residual Correlation Matrix...\n")

# Extract candidate theta scores (EAP)
theta_scores <- fscores(fit_2pl, method = 'EAP')
pars_2pl     <- coef(fit_2pl, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

# Calculate expected probability matrix (P_ij)
theta_mat <- matrix(theta_scores[, 1], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix))
a_vec     <- matrix(pars_2pl[, "a"], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix), byrow = TRUE)
b_vec     <- matrix(pars_2pl[, "b"], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix), byrow = TRUE)

P_mat   <- 1 / (1 + exp(-a_vec * (theta_mat - b_vec)))
res_mat <- clean_matrix - P_mat

# Pairwise residual correlation matrix
q3_matrix <- cor(res_mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
q3_values <- q3_matrix[upper.tri(q3_matrix)]

q3_summary_df <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Mean Q3 Correlation", "Max Q3 Correlation", "Total Pairs Evaluated", "Pairs Q3 > 0.20"),
  Value  = c(
    round(mean(q3_values, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(max(q3_values, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    length(q3_values),
    sum(q3_values > 0.20, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("\n=== LOCAL INDEPENDENCE SUMMARY (2PL) ===\n")
print(q3_summary_df)

# ======================================================================
# STEP 6: EXTRACT ITEM PARAMETERS & PERSON SCORES FOR 2PL

# 1. Summary table for 2PL item parameters
summary_2pl_items <- data.frame(
  Item         = rownames(pars_2pl),
  Slope_a      = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "a"]), 3),
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "b"]), 3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Extract EAP person scores from fit_2pl_active
fscores_2pl <- fscores(
  fit_2pl, 
  method = 'EAP', 
  full.scores = TRUE, 
  full.scores.SE = TRUE
)

theta_vec <- as.numeric(fscores_2pl[, "F1"])
se_vec    <- as.numeric(fscores_2pl[, "SE_F1"])

# Initialize NA template columns in Master Dataset
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_Theta <- NA_real_
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_SE    <- NA_real_

# Identify exact row positions scored by mirt
scored_indices <- which(
  rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0 & 
  apply(clean_matrix, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
)

# Fallback if variance criteria length varies slightly
if (length(scored_indices) != length(theta_vec)) {
  scored_indices <- which(rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0)[1:length(theta_vec)]
}

# Assign Theta and SE safely to Master Dataset
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_Theta[scored_indices] <- theta_vec
CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_SE[scored_indices]    <- se_vec

cat("\nSuccessfully assigned 2PL Theta and SE to Master Dataset.\n")
cat("Master Dataset total rows:", nrow(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025), "\n")
cat("Scored candidates assigned:", sum(!is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_Theta)), "\n")

# Verify alignment correlation
raw_scores <- rowSums(clean_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_idx  <- !is.na(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_Theta)

alignment_corr <- cor(
  raw_scores[valid_idx], 
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_2PL_Theta[valid_idx], 
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cat("Alignment Check — Correlation between Raw Sum Score and 2PL Theta:", round(alignment_corr, 4), "\n")

# ======================================================================
# STEP 7: DIAGNOSTIC PLOTS
plot(fit_2pl, type = 'trace', main = '2PL Item Trace Lines')
plot(fit_2pl, type = 'infotrace', main = '2PL Item Information Curves')
plot(fit_2pl, type = 'infoSE', main = 'Test Information & SE')

# ======================================================================
# STEP 8: EXCEL EXPORT VIA OPENXLSX
cat("\nExporting results to Excel workbook...\n")

wb <- createWorkbook()

# Sheet 1: Model Comparative Summary (M2 & ANOVA)
addWorksheet(wb, "Model_Comparison")
writeData(wb, "Model_Comparison", "GLOBAL M2 FIT INDICES", startCol = 1, startRow = 1)
writeDataTable(wb, "Model_Comparison", unidim_fit_summary, startCol = 1, startRow = 2, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")

writeData(wb, "Model_Comparison", "MODEL COMPARISON (ANOVA / AIC / BIC)", startCol = 1, startRow = 8)
writeDataTable(wb, "Model_Comparison", model_comp_df, startCol = 1, startRow = 9, rowNames = TRUE, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
setColWidths(wb, "Model_Comparison", cols = 1:ncol(unidim_fit_summary), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 2: 2PL Item Parameters
addWorksheet(wb, "2PL_Item_Parameters")
writeDataTable(wb, "2PL_Item_Parameters", summary_2pl_items, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
setColWidths(wb, "2PL_Item_Parameters", cols = 1:ncol(summary_2pl_items), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 3: Candidate Person Scores
export_participant_df <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025 %>% 
  dplyr::select(any_of(c(id_var, "timecompleted", "year_completed", "Active_2PL_Theta", "Active_2PL_SE")))

addWorksheet(wb, "Candidate_Scores")
writeDataTable(wb, "Candidate_Scores", export_participant_df, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
setColWidths(wb, "Candidate_Scores", cols = 1:ncol(export_participant_df), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 4: Local Independence (Q3 Summary)
addWorksheet(wb, "Local_Independence_Q3")
writeDataTable(wb, "Local_Independence_Q3", q3_summary_df, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
setColWidths(wb, "Local_Independence_Q3", cols = 1:ncol(q3_summary_df), widths = "auto")

# Save Workbook
excel_filename <- "IRT_Active_2PL_Analysis_Results.xlsx"
saveWorkbook(wb, excel_filename, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("\n==================================================================\n")
cat("SUCCESS! Analysis complete and saved to:", excel_filename, "\n")
cat("==================================================================\n")
```

#### Identify the Highest-Correlated Item Pairs

To see which specific items are violating local independence, run this block to pull the top dependent pairs:

(R script to identify all item pairs violating Local Independence ($Q_3 > 0.20$), list every unique item involved in a violation, count how many times each item appears in a violating pair, and export the flagged items and pairs directly for test refinement.

In Yen's $Q_3$ analysis, centering $Q_3$ values around their average (since the expected value of $Q_3$ under local independence is slightly negative, approx. $-1/(N_{\text{items}}-1)$) is often standard practice, but evaluating raw $Q_3 > 0.20$ or adjusted $Q_3^* > 0.20$ directly identifies the worst offending pairs.)

```{r}
#| label: item-pair-correlations
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# 1. PROCESS Q3 MATRIX INTO DISTINCT PAIRS
# ==============================================================================
q3_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(q3_matrix)) %>%
  filter(Var1 != Var2) %>%
  mutate(
    Item1 = pmin(as.character(Var1), as.character(Var2)),
    Item2 = pmax(as.character(Var1), as.character(Var2))
  ) %>%
  distinct(Item1, Item2, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  rename(Q3_Correlation = Freq) %>%
  arrange(desc(Q3_Correlation))

# ==============================================================================
# 2. FILTER ALL PAIRS VIOLATING LOCAL INDEPENDENCE (Q3 > 0.20)
 
q3_cutoff <- 0.20

q3_violations <- q3_long %>%
  filter(Q3_Correlation > q3_cutoff)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. IDENTIFY ALL UNIQUE ITEMS VIOLATING LOCAL INDEPENDENCE & COUNT FREQUENCY
 
violating_items_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(q3_violations$Item1, q3_violations$Item2)
) %>%
  group_by(Item) %>%
  summarise(
    Violation_Count = n(),
    Max_Q3_Value   = NA_real_, # Populated below
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Violation_Count))

# Add max Q3 correlation per item for prioritization
for (i in seq_len(nrow(violating_items_summary))) {
  itm <- violating_items_summary$Item[i]
  max_q3 <- q3_violations %>%
    filter(Item1 == itm | Item2 == itm) %>%
    summarise(m = max(Q3_Correlation)) %>%
    pull(m)
  violating_items_summary$Max_Q3_Value[i] <- round(max_q3, 4)
}

# ============================================================
# 4. PRINT DIAGNOSTIC RESULTS TO CONSOLE
 
cat("==================================================================\n")
cat("LOCAL INDEPENDENCE VIOLATION SUMMARY (Cutoff: Q3 >", q3_cutoff, ")\n")
cat("==================================================================\n\n")

cat("Total Item Pairs Evaluated:            ", nrow(q3_long), "\n")
cat("Total Dependent Pairs (Q3 > 0.20):     ", nrow(q3_violations), "\n")
cat("Total Unique Flagged Items:            ", nrow(violating_items_summary), "\n\n")

cat("--- TOP FLAGGED ITEMS RANKED BY VIOLATION FREQUENCY ---\n")
if (nrow(violating_items_summary) > 0) {
  # Only print the top 15 worst items to keep the console clean
  print(knitr::kable(head(violating_items_summary, 15)))
  cat("\n(Note: The full list of items and all violating pairs have been exported to Excel.)\n")
} else {
  cat("No items flagged.\n")
}

# ======================================================================
# 5. EXPORT RESULTS TO EXCEL FOR ITEM SELECTION & PRUNING

wb_q3 <- createWorkbook()

# Sheet 1: Item-Level Violation Counts (Prioritize which items to drop first)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary", violating_items_summary, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary", cols = 1:ncol(violating_items_summary), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 2: All Violating Pairs (Q3 > 0.20)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20", q3_violations, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20", cols = 1:ncol(q3_violations), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 3: Full Ranked Q3 Correlations Matrix (Long)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked", q3_long, tableStyle = "TableStyleLight1")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked", cols = 1:ncol(q3_long), widths = "auto")

excel_q3_out <- "IRT_Local_Independence_Q3_Violations.xlsx"
saveWorkbook(wb_q3, excel_q3_out, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("\n==================================================================\n")
cat("SUCCESS! Q3 local independence analysis saved to:\n", excel_q3_out, "\n")
cat("==================================================================\n")
```

## 5. Compare performance of the models

### Evaluating the Results

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| **Statistic** | **Good Fit Threshold** | **What it Tells You** |
| **RMSEA** | $< 0.06$ (acceptable $< 0.08$) | Root Mean Square Error of Approximation; indicates closeness to unidimensional fit. |
| **CFI / TLI** | $> 0.95$ (acceptable $> 0.90$) | Comparative Fit Index / Tucker-Lewis Index; values above $0.95$ strongly support a single dimension. |
| **AIC / BIC** | **Lowest Value** Wins | Penalizes model complexity. Select the model with the lowest AIC/BIC. |
| $p$-value (LRT) | $p < 0.05$ | If significant when comparing 1PL vs 2PL, freeing discrimination parameters (2PL) significantly improves fit. |
| **Q3 Violations** | Pairwise $Q_3 < 0.20$ | Residual correlations above $0.20$ point to pairs of items that violate local independence (suggesting secondary dimensions). |

```{r}
 #| label: model-performance-comparison
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# 1. Verify convergence for all three models (Should all return TRUE)
cat("Rasch Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_rasch, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("1PL Converged:  ", extract.mirt(fit_1pl, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("2PL Converged:  ", extract.mirt(fit_2pl, 'converged'), "\n\n")

# 2. Compare Model Fit via Likelihood Ratio Test (ANOVA)
# Nested comparison: Rasch (slopes = 1) vs 1PL (common slope) vs 2PL (unique slopes)
model_comp <- anova(fit_rasch, fit_1pl, fit_2pl)

# 3. Format and display with kable
kable(model_comp, caption = "Model Fit Comparison: Rasch vs 1PL vs 2PL")
```

Model comparison is made based on the separate model estimations, separate number of items. Exact match of items (meeting the 500 response limits for 2PL) produce the following results:

```{r}
#| label: irt-model-comparison-aligned
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. BUILD ONE SHARED MATRIX FOR ALL THREE MODELS (IDENTICAL ITEMS & ROWS)
min_n_cmp <- 500

item_n_cmp   <- colSums(!is.na(mirt_active_matrix))
item_var_cmp <- apply(mirt_active_matrix, 2, stats::var, na.rm = TRUE)
cmp_items    <- names(item_n_cmp)[item_n_cmp >= min_n_cmp & !is.na(item_var_cmp) & item_var_cmp > 0]

stopifnot(length(cmp_items) >= 2)

mirt_cmp_sub    <- mirt_active_matrix[, cmp_items, drop = FALSE]
keep_rows_cmp   <- rowSums(!is.na(mirt_cmp_sub)) > 0
mirt_cmp_matrix <- mirt_cmp_sub[keep_rows_cmp, , drop = FALSE]

cat(sprintf(
  "Shared comparison matrix: %d respondents x %d items (min N >= %d)\n",
  nrow(mirt_cmp_matrix), ncol(mirt_cmp_matrix), min_n_cmp
))

# 2. DEFINE TRUE 1PL MODEL (EQUAL SLOPES 'a1' ACROSS ALL ITEMS, FREE LATENT VARIANCE)
n_cmp_items <- ncol(mirt_cmp_matrix)
spec_1pl <- mirt::mirt.model(sprintf(
  "F = 1-%d
   CONSTRAIN = (1-%d, a1)
   COV = F1*F1",
  n_cmp_items, n_cmp_items
))

# 3. FIT RASCH, TRUE 1PL, AND 2PL ON THE EXACT SAME DATA
fit_cmp_rasch <- mirt::mirt(
  data = mirt_cmp_matrix, model = 1, itemtype = "Rasch",
  quadpts = 21, TOL = 0.001, technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), verbose = FALSE
)

fit_cmp_1pl <- mirt::mirt(
  data = mirt_cmp_matrix, model = spec_1pl, itemtype = "2PL",
  quadpts = 21, TOL = 0.001, technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), verbose = FALSE
)

fit_cmp_2pl <- mirt::mirt(
  data = mirt_cmp_matrix, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL",
  quadpts = 21, TOL = 0.001, technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), verbose = FALSE
)

# 4. PAIRWISE LIKELIHOOD-RATIO COMPARISON USING mirt::anova()
lr_rasch_2pl <- mirt::anova(fit_cmp_rasch, fit_cmp_2pl, verbose = FALSE)
lr_1pl_2pl   <- mirt::anova(fit_cmp_1pl,   fit_cmp_2pl, verbose = FALSE)

cmp_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Model     = c("Rasch", "True 1PL (Equal Slopes)", "2PL"),
  Converged = c(
    mirt::extract.mirt(fit_cmp_rasch, "converged"),
    mirt::extract.mirt(fit_cmp_1pl,   "converged"),
    mirt::extract.mirt(fit_cmp_2pl,   "converged")
  ),
  AIC       = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$AIC[1],   lr_1pl_2pl$AIC[1],   lr_rasch_2pl$AIC[2]), 1),
  SABIC     = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$SABIC[1], lr_1pl_2pl$SABIC[1], lr_rasch_2pl$SABIC[2]), 1),
  HQ        = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$HQ[1],    lr_1pl_2pl$HQ[1],    lr_rasch_2pl$HQ[2]), 1),
  BIC       = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$BIC[1],   lr_1pl_2pl$BIC[1],   lr_rasch_2pl$BIC[2]), 1),
  logLik    = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$logLik[1],lr_1pl_2pl$logLik[1],lr_rasch_2pl$logLik[2]), 1),
  X2_vs_2PL = round(c(lr_rasch_2pl$X2[2],    lr_1pl_2pl$X2[2],    NA_real_), 2),
  df_vs_2PL = c(lr_rasch_2pl$df[2],          lr_1pl_2pl$df[2],          NA_integer_),
  p_vs_2PL  = c(
    ifelse(is.na(lr_rasch_2pl$p[2]), NA_character_, format.pval(lr_rasch_2pl$p[2], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)),
    ifelse(is.na(lr_1pl_2pl$p[2]),   NA_character_, format.pval(lr_1pl_2pl$p[2],   digits = 3, eps = 0.001)),
    NA_character_
  )
)

knitr::kable(cmp_table, caption = sprintf("Aligned 2025 IRT Model Comparison (N >= %d items)", min_n_cmp))
```

This aligned comparison gives clearer picture of three models. Rasch and 1PL model have identical fit indices. 2PL has a substantially better model fit than both Rasch and 1PL because item discrimination parameter varies across (common) items. This means using just difficulty parameter is not able to capture how the items separate high and low ability candidates. Because $\chi^2$ is sensitive to large sample sizesBIC and SABIC are the main parameters to consider.

### Compare Item Discrimination & Difficulty Parameters

```{r}
#| label: model-parameter-comparison
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. HELPER TO EXTRACT KEYED ITEM PARAMETERS SAFELY
extract_irt_df <- function(fit_obj, prefix) {
  pars <- mirt::coef(fit_obj, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items
  tibble::tibble(
    Item                   = rownames(pars),
    !!paste0(prefix, "_a") := round(as.numeric(pars[, "a"]), 3),
    !!paste0(prefix, "_b") := round(as.numeric(pars[, "b"]), 3)
  )
}

df_rasch <- extract_irt_df(fit_rasch, "Rasch")
df_1pl   <- extract_irt_df(fit_1pl,   "1PL")
df_2pl   <- extract_irt_df(fit_2pl,   "2PL")

cat(sprintf(
  "2025 Examinees: %d | Calibrated Items -> Rasch: %d | 1PL: %d | 2PL: %d\n",
```

```{r}
#| label: theta-cross-model-comparison

theta_cols <- intersect(
  c("Rasch_Theta", "Theta_1PL", "Theta_2PL"),
  names(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)
)

stopifnot(length(theta_cols) >= 2)

theta_mat <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[, theta_cols, drop = FALSE]

# 1. CORRELATION MATRIX ACROSS MODELS
theta_correlations <- stats::cor(theta_mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cat("=== CORRELATION AMONG PERSON THETA ESTIMATES ===\n")
print(round(theta_correlations, 4))

# 2. PAIRWISE MEAN ABSOLUTE & ROOT MEAN SQUARE DIFFERENCES (PRACTICAL AGREEMENT)
pairs_df <- utils::combn(theta_cols, 2, simplify = FALSE)
diff_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs_df, function(p) {
  x <- theta_mat[[p[1]]]
  y <- theta_mat[[p[2]]]
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  data.frame(
    Pair = paste(p[1], "vs.", p[2]),
    N    = sum(ok),
    r    = round(stats::cor(x[ok], y[ok]), 4),
    MAE  = round(mean(abs(x[ok] - y[ok])), 4),
    RMSE = round(sqrt(mean((x[ok] - y[ok])^2)), 4),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(diff_summary, caption = "Person Ability (Theta) Agreement Across Models")
```

## 6. Adverse Impact

Adverse impact analysis has been carried out based on current percentiles to start with. Detailed analysis for all diversity groups has been performed using the new 1PL model estimation. 1PL was selected because it is the same model used at the moment and is the best performing model, though the other two (Rasch and 2PL) have very similar outcomes.

6.  Frequencies of Diversity Groups

```{r}
#| label: Frequencies of Diversity Groups
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. Convert Master Dataset to a clean standard data.frame
df_clean <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)

demographic_vars <- c("gender", "select_your_ethnicity", "select_your_current_age_group", "disability", "application_form_applicant_type", "job_grade", "what_is_your_sexual_orientation", "were_you_eligible_for_free_school_meals_at_any_point", "what_is_your_religion_or_belief" ) # Replace/add your demographic column names 

grade_var        <- "job_grade"            # Replace with your actual job grade column name

# Helper function: Safely flattens a column if it is stored as a list
clean_vector_col <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) {
    sapply(x, function(val) {
      if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0 || all(is.na(val))) {
        return(NA_character_)
      } else {
        return(as.character(val[[1]])) # Extract first scalar element
      }
    })
  } else {
    return(as.character(x))
  }
}

# Clean grade column
if (grade_var %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
  df_clean[[grade_var]] <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[grade_var]])
}

# ==============================================================================
# 1. OVERALL DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES (TOTAL SAMPLE)

cat("=== OVERALL DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES (N = ", nrow(df_clean), ") ===\n\n")

for (demo in demographic_vars) {
  if (demo %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
    
    # Flatten list-column if necessary
    demo_vec <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[demo]])
    
    overall_counts <- data.frame(Group = demo_vec, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(Group = ifelse(is.na(Group) | Group == "", "Missing/NA", Group)) %>%
      group_by(Group) %>%
      summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(
        Percent = round((N / sum(N)) * 100, 2),
        Cumulative_N = cumsum(N)
      ) %>%
      rename(!!sym(demo) := Group)
    
    print(kable(overall_counts, caption = paste("Overall Breakdown:", demo)))
    cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  } else {
    warning(paste("Variable", demo, "not found in master dataset!"))
  }
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES BY JOB GRADE (CROSS-TABULATION)

cat("\n=== DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES BY JOB GRADE ===\n\n")

for (demo in demographic_vars) {
  if (demo %in% colnames(df_clean) && grade_var %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
    
    # Extract flattened character vectors
    demo_clean_vec  <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[demo]])
    grade_clean_vec <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[grade_var]])
    
    cross_tab_counts <- data.frame(
      Grade = ifelse(is.na(grade_clean_vec) | grade_clean_vec == "", "Missing_Grade", grade_clean_vec),
      Demo  = ifelse(is.na(demo_clean_vec) | demo_clean_vec == "", "Missing/NA", demo_clean_vec),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ) %>%
      group_by(Grade, Demo) %>%
      summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
      mutate(Percent_Within_Grade = round((N / sum(N)) * 100, 2)) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    # Pivot N Counts Table
    counts_wide <- cross_tab_counts %>%
      dplyr::select(Grade, Demo, N) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = Demo, values_from = N, values_fill = 0) %>%
      rename(!!sym(grade_var) := Grade)
    
    cat("\n--- Headcount Breakdown (N):", grade_var, "x", demo, "---\n")
    print(kable(counts_wide))
    
    # Pivot Percentage Table
    pct_wide <- cross_tab_counts %>%
      dplyr::select(Grade, Demo, Percent_Within_Grade) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = Demo, values_from = Percent_Within_Grade, values_fill = 0) %>%
      rename(!!sym(grade_var) := Grade)
    
    cat("\n--- Percentage Breakdown (% within Grade):", grade_var, "x", demo, "---\n")
    print(kable(pct_wide))
    cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  }
}
```

### 6.A Gender

```{r}
#| label: gender-adverse-impact-1pl
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. SETUP & FILTER DATASET
target_grades <- c("Administrative Officer", "Executive Officer", "Higher Executive Office",
                   "Senior Executive Office", "Grade7", "Grade 6")

clean_vec <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) vapply(x, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
  else as.character(x)
}

gender_col <- intersect(c("gender", "Gender"), colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))[1]
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

df_gender <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    grade = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Administrative Officer") ~ "Administrative Officer",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Executive Officer")      ~ "Executive Officer",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Higher Executive")       ~ "Higher Executive Office",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Senior Executive")       ~ "Senior Executive Office",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?7")               ~ "Grade7",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?6")               ~ "Grade 6"
    ),
    gender = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(stringr::str_trim(clean_vec(.data[[gender_col]])), "(?i)^(man|men|male|m|0)$")       ~ "Man",
      stringr::str_detect(stringr::str_trim(clean_vec(.data[[gender_col]])), "(?i)^(woman|women|female|f|1)$") ~ "Woman"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(grade), !is.na(gender)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    grade = factor(grade, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile_1PL = pmax(1, ceiling(dplyr::percent_rank(Theta_1PL) * 100))
  )

# 2. VECTORIZED ADVERSE IMPACT GRID BUILDER
build_ai_grid <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
  totals <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(grade, gender, name = "total") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = total, values_fill = 0)
  
  tidyr::expand_grid(grade = factor(target_grades, levels = target_grades), Percentile = 1:100, gender = c("Man", "Woman")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      data %>% dplyr::group_by(grade, Percentile = .data[[pct_col]], gender) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), avg_th = mean(.data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("grade", "Percentile", "gender")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(n = tidyr::replace_na(n, 0)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = c(n, avg_th)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(totals, by = "grade") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Man   = tidyr::replace_na(Man, 0),
      Woman = tidyr::replace_na(Woman, 0)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grade) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Percentile), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Man_Avg_Theta              = round(avg_th_Man, 4),
      Woman_Avg_Theta            = round(avg_th_Woman, 4),
      Theta_Diff_Woman_minus_Man = round(avg_th_Woman - avg_th_Man, 4),
      Impact_Ratio_AIR           = round(
        ifelse(Man >= 5 & Woman >= 5 & cumsum(n_Man) > 0, (cumsum(n_Woman) / Woman) / (cumsum(n_Man) / Man), NA_real_),
        3
      ),
      Adverse_Impact_Flag        = dplyr::case_when(
        Man < 5 | Woman < 5     ~ "Insufficient Data (n < 5)",
        is.na(Impact_Ratio_AIR) ~ "N/A",
        Impact_Ratio_AIR < 0.80 ~ "YES (AIR < 0.80)",
        TRUE                    ~ "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(grade, Percentile) %>%
    dplyr::select(grade, Percentile, Man_Count = n_Man, Woman_Count = n_Woman, Man_Avg_Theta, Woman_Avg_Theta, Theta_Diff_Woman_minus_Man, Impact_Ratio_AIR, Adverse_Impact_Flag) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = grade, values_from = -c(grade, Percentile), names_glue = "{gsub(' ', '_', grade)}_{.value}")
}

# 3. SUMMARIZE ADVERSE IMPACT ONSET PERCENTILE PER GRADE (1PL ONLY)
grid_1pl <- build_ai_grid(df_gender, "Theta_1PL", "Percentile_1PL")

grade_counts <- df_gender %>%
  dplyr::count(grade, gender) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

ai_onset_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(target_grades, \(g) {
  prefix   <- gsub(" ", "_", g)
  air_col  <- paste0(prefix, "_Impact_Ratio_AIR")
  
  n_man   <- grade_counts$Man[grade_counts$grade == g]
  n_woman <- grade_counts$Woman[grade_counts$grade == g]
  n_man   <- if (length(n_man) == 0) 0 else n_man
  n_woman <- if (length(n_woman) == 0) 0 else n_woman
  
  insufficient <- (n_man < 5 | n_woman < 5)
  ai_rows      <- grid_1pl %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[air_col]]) & .data[[air_col]] < 0.80)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model        = "1PL Theta",
    Job_Grade    = g,
    Man_n        = n_man,
    Woman_n      = n_woman,
    AI_Onset_Pct = dplyr::case_when(
      insufficient      ~ "Insufficient data (n < 5)",
      nrow(ai_rows) > 0 ~ paste0("Starts at ", min(ai_rows$Percentile), "th percentile"),
      TRUE              ~ "No Adverse Impact"
    ),
    AIR_at_Onset = if (!insufficient && nrow(ai_rows) > 0) ai_rows[[air_col]][which.min(ai_rows$Percentile)] else NA_real_,
    Min_AIR      = if (!insufficient) round(min(grid_1pl[[air_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_
  )
})

# 4. EXPORT TO EXCEL & PRINT TABLE IN QUARTO
sheets <- list(
  "1PL_Theta_Gender_AI" = grid_1pl,
  "AI_Onset_Summary"    = ai_onset_summary
)

wb_gender <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
invisible(purrr::imap(sheets, \(df, nm) {
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb_gender, nm)
  openxlsx::writeDataTable(wb_gender, nm, df)
  openxlsx::setColWidths(wb_gender, nm, 1:ncol(df), "auto")
}))
openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb_gender, "CSNT_Gender_Theta_Adverse_Impact_By_Percentile.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

knitr::kable(ai_onset_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: disability-adverse-impact-1pl

# 1. SETUP & FILTER DATASET (DISABILITY - 1PL ONLY)
target_grades <- c("Administrative Officer", "Executive Officer", "Higher Executive Office",
                   "Senior Executive Office", "Grade7", "Grade 6")

min_n_threshold <- 5  # Minimum group size per percentile required to evaluate AIR reliably

clean_vec <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) {
    vapply(x, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
  } else {
    as.character(x)
  }
}

dis_col <- intersect(c("disability", "disability.y", "disability.x"), colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))[1]
stopifnot(!is.na(dis_col))

if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

df_dis <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Theta_1PL = as.numeric(Theta_1PL),
    grade = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Administrative Officer") ~ "Administrative Officer",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Executive Officer")      ~ "Executive Officer",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Higher Executive")       ~ "Higher Executive Office",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Senior Executive")       ~ "Senior Executive Office",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?7")               ~ "Grade7",
      stringr::str_detect(clean_vec(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?6")               ~ "Grade 6"
    ),
    dis = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(stringr::str_trim(clean_vec(.data[[dis_col]])), "(?i)^(no|non[- ]?disabled|0)$") ~ "No",
      stringr::str_detect(stringr::str_trim(clean_vec(.data[[dis_col]])), "(?i)^(yes|disabled|1)$")        ~ "Yes"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(grade), !is.na(dis), !is.na(Theta_1PL)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    grade          = factor(grade, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile_1PL = pmax(1, ceiling(dplyr::percent_rank(Theta_1PL) * 100))
  )

# 2. VECTORIZED ADVERSE IMPACT GRID BUILDER (Strict < 5 Per-Percentile Guardrail)
build_ai_grid_dis <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
  totals <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(grade, dis, name = "total") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = dis, values_from = total, values_fill = 0)
  
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    grade      = factor(target_grades, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile = 1:100,
    dis        = c("No", "Yes")
  ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(grade, Percentile = .data[[pct_col]], dis) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), avg_th = mean(.data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("grade", "Percentile", "dis")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(n = tidyr::replace_na(n, 0)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = dis, values_from = c(n, avg_th)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(totals, by = "grade") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      No  = tidyr::replace_na(No, 0L),
      Yes = tidyr::replace_na(Yes, 0L)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grade) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Percentile), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      cum_No  = cumsum(n_No),
      cum_Yes = cumsum(n_Yes),
      has_enough_data = !is.na(No) & !is.na(Yes) &
                        No >= min_n_threshold & Yes >= min_n_threshold &
                        n_No >= min_n_threshold & n_Yes >= min_n_threshold &
                        cum_No >= min_n_threshold & cum_Yes >= min_n_threshold,
      No_Avg_Theta            = ifelse(n_No >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_No, 4), NA_real_),
      Yes_Avg_Theta           = ifelse(n_Yes >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_Yes, 4), NA_real_),
      Theta_Diff_Yes_minus_No = ifelse(
        n_No >= min_n_threshold & n_Yes >= min_n_threshold,
        round(avg_th_Yes - avg_th_No, 4),
        NA_real_
      ),
      Impact_Ratio_AIR        = ifelse(
        has_enough_data,
        round((cum_Yes / Yes) / (cum_No / No), 3),
        NA_real_
      ),
      Adverse_Impact_Flag     = dplyr::case_when(
        !has_enough_data        ~ "Insufficient Data",
        Impact_Ratio_AIR < 0.80 ~ "YES (AIR < 0.80)",
        TRUE                    ~ "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(grade, Percentile) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      grade, Percentile,
      No_Count = n_No, Yes_Count = n_Yes,
      No_Avg_Theta, Yes_Avg_Theta, Theta_Diff_Yes_minus_No,
      Impact_Ratio_AIR, Adverse_Impact_Flag
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from  = grade,
      values_from = -c(grade, Percentile),
      names_glue  = "{gsub(' ', '_', grade)}_{.value}"
    )
}

# 3. SUMMARIZE ADVERSE IMPACT ONSET PERCENTILE PER GRADE (Handling Insufficient Data Cleanly)
grid_1pl_dis <- build_ai_grid_dis(df_dis, "Theta_1PL", "Percentile_1PL")

ai_onset_dis <- purrr::map_dfr(target_grades, \(g) {
  prefix   <- gsub(" ", "_", g)
  air_col  <- paste0(prefix, "_Impact_Ratio_AIR")
  flag_col <- paste0(prefix, "_Adverse_Impact_Flag")
  
  valid_rows <- grid_1pl_dis %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[flag_col]] != "Insufficient Data")
  ai_rows    <- valid_rows %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[air_col]] < 0.80)
  insuff_pct <- grid_1pl_dis %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[flag_col]] == "Insufficient Data") %>% dplyr::pull(Percentile)
  
  onset_text <- if (nrow(valid_rows) == 0) {
    "Insufficient Data"
  } else if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) {
    paste0("Starts at ", min(ai_rows$Percentile), "th percentile")
  } else {
    "No Adverse Impact"
  }
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model             = "1PL Theta",
    Job_Grade         = g,
    AI_Onset_Pct      = onset_text,
    AIR_at_Onset      = if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) ai_rows[[air_col]][which.min(ai_rows$Percentile)] else NA_real_,
    Min_Valid_AIR     = if (nrow(valid_rows) > 0) round(min(valid_rows[[air_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_,
    Insufficient_Pcts = if (length(insuff_pct) > 0) paste0(min(insuff_pct), "th–", max(insuff_pct), "th pct") else "None"
  )
})

# 4. EXPORT TO EXCEL & PRINT TABLE IN QUARTO
sheets_dis <- list(
  "1PL_Theta_Disability_AI" = grid_1pl_dis,
  "AI_Onset_Summary"        = ai_onset_dis
)

wb_dis <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
invisible(purrr::imap(sheets_dis, \(df, nm) {
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb_dis, nm)
  openxlsx::writeDataTable(wb_dis, nm, df)
  openxlsx::setColWidths(wb_dis, nm, 1:ncol(df), "auto")
}))
openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb_dis, "CSNT_JobGrade_Disability_Theta_Adverse_Impact_By_Percentile.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

knitr::kable(ai_onset_dis)
```

No adverse impact is present for Disability. Insufficient Data is presented where the number of persons per group is lower than 5.

```{r}
#| label: ethnicity-adverse-impact-1pl

# 1. SETUP & FILTER DATASET (ETHNICITY - 1PL ONLY)
target_grades <- c("Administrative Officer", "Executive Officer", "Higher Executive Office",
                   "Senior Executive Office", "Grade7", "Grade 6")

focal_ethnicities <- c(
  "Asian / Asian British",
  "Black / African / Caribbean / Black British",
  "Mixed / multiple ethnic groups",
  "Other ethnic group"
)

min_n_threshold <- 5  # Minimum group size required to evaluate AIR reliably (< 5 -> Insufficient Data)

clean_vec <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) {
    vapply(x, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
  } else {
    x
  }
}

eth_col <- intersect(c("select_your_ethnic_group", "select_your_ethnic_group.y", "select_your_ethnic_group.x"), 
                     colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025))[1]
stopifnot(!is.na(eth_col))

if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

# Flatten ALL list-columns upfront and coerce Theta_1PL to numeric
df_raw <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025) %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.list), clean_vec),
    Theta_1PL = as.numeric(Theta_1PL)
  )

df_eth <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    grade = case_when(
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Administrative Officer") ~ "Administrative Officer",
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Executive Officer")      ~ "Executive Officer",
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Higher Executive")       ~ "Higher Executive Office",
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Senior Executive")       ~ "Senior Executive Office",
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?7")               ~ "Grade7",
      str_detect(as.character(job_grade), "(?i)Grade ?6")               ~ "Grade 6"
    ),
    eth_raw = str_trim(as.character(.data[[eth_col]])),
    eth = case_when(
      str_detect(eth_raw, "(?i)^white") ~ "White",
      eth_raw %in% focal_ethnicities | str_detect(eth_raw, "(?i)^(asian|black|mixed|other ethnic)") ~ "Others",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade), !is.na(eth), !is.na(Theta_1PL)) %>%
  mutate(
    grade          = factor(grade, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile_1PL = pmax(1, ceiling(percent_rank(Theta_1PL) * 100))
  )

# 2. VECTORIZED ADVERSE IMPACT GRID BUILDER (Strict < 5 Guardrail)
build_ai_grid_eth <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
  totals <- data %>% 
    dplyr::count(grade, eth, name = "total") %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = eth, values_from = total, values_fill = 0)
  
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    grade      = factor(target_grades, levels = target_grades), 
    Percentile = 1:100, 
    eth        = c("White", "Others")
  ) %>%
    left_join(
      data %>% 
        group_by(grade, Percentile = .data[[pct_col]], eth) %>%
        summarise(n = n(), avg_th = mean(.data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("grade", "Percentile", "eth")
    ) %>%
    mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = eth, values_from = c(n, avg_th)) %>%
    left_join(totals, by = "grade") %>%
    mutate(
      White  = replace_na(White, 0L),
      Others = replace_na(Others, 0L)
    ) %>%
    group_by(grade) %>%
    arrange(desc(Percentile), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      cum_White  = cumsum(n_White),
      cum_Others = cumsum(n_Others),
      has_enough_data = !is.na(White) & !is.na(Others) &
                        White >= min_n_threshold & Others >= min_n_threshold &
                        n_White >= min_n_threshold & n_Others >= min_n_threshold &
                        cum_White >= min_n_threshold & cum_Others >= min_n_threshold,
      White_Avg_Theta              = ifelse(n_White >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_White, 4), NA_real_),
      Others_Avg_Theta             = ifelse(n_Others >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_Others, 4), NA_real_),
      Theta_Diff_Others_minus_Wht  = ifelse(
        n_White >= min_n_threshold & n_Others >= min_n_threshold, 
        round(avg_th_Others - avg_th_White, 4), 
        NA_real_
      ),
      Impact_Ratio_AIR             = ifelse(
        has_enough_data, 
        round((cum_Others / Others) / (cum_White / White), 3), 
        NA_real_
      ),
      Adverse_Impact_Flag          = case_when(
        !has_enough_data        ~ "Insufficient Data",
        Impact_Ratio_AIR < 0.80 ~ "YES (AIR < 0.80)",
        TRUE                    ~ "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(grade, Percentile) %>%
    select(grade, Percentile, White_Count = n_White, Others_Count = n_Others, 
           White_Avg_Theta, Others_Avg_Theta, Theta_Diff_Others_minus_Wht, 
           Impact_Ratio_AIR, Adverse_Impact_Flag) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = grade, values_from = -c(grade, Percentile), names_glue = "{gsub(' ', '_', grade)}_{.value}")
}

# 3. SUMMARIZE ADVERSE IMPACT ONSET PERCENTILE (Handling Insufficient Data cleanly)
summarize_ai_onset_eth <- function(grid_df, model_label = "1PL Theta") {
  map_dfr(target_grades, \(g) {
    prefix   <- gsub(" ", "_", g)
    air_col  <- paste0(prefix, "_Impact_Ratio_AIR")
    flag_col <- paste0(prefix, "_Adverse_Impact_Flag")
    
    valid_rows <- grid_df %>% filter(.data[[flag_col]] != "Insufficient Data")
    ai_rows    <- valid_rows %>% filter(.data[[air_col]] < 0.80)
    insuff_pct <- grid_df %>% filter(.data[[flag_col]] == "Insufficient Data") %>% pull(Percentile)
    
    onset_text <- if (nrow(valid_rows) == 0) {
      "Insufficient Data"
    } else if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) {
      paste0("Starts at ", min(ai_rows$Percentile), "th percentile")
    } else {
      "No Adverse Impact"
    }
    
    tibble(
      Model             = model_label,
      Job_Grade         = g,
      AI_Onset_Pct      = onset_text,
      AIR_at_Onset      = if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) ai_rows[[air_col]][which.min(ai_rows$Percentile)] else NA_real_,
      Min_Valid_AIR     = if (nrow(valid_rows) > 0) round(min(valid_rows[[air_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_,
      Insufficient_Pcts = if (length(insuff_pct) > 0) paste0(min(insuff_pct), "th–", max(insuff_pct), "th pct") else "None"
    )
  })
}

# 4. GENERATE TABLES, DISPLAY ONSET SUMMARY & EXPORT TO EXCEL
```

```{r}
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {

    ),
```

```{r}
    age_grp = case_when(

    )
```
