```{r}
# 2. VECTORIZED ADVERSE IMPACT GRID BUILDER (With Sparse-Data Guardrail)
build_ai_grid_age <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
  totals <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(grade, age_grp, name = "total") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = age_grp, values_from = total, values_fill = 0)
  
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    grade      = factor(target_grades, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile = 1:100,
    age_grp    = c("Under40", "40andOver")
  ) %>%
    left_join(
      data %>%
        group_by(grade, Percentile = .data[[pct_col]], age_grp) %>%
        summarise(n = n(), avg_th = mean(.data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("grade", "Percentile", "age_grp")
    ) %>%
    mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = age_grp, values_from = c(n, avg_th)) %>%
    left_join(totals, by = "grade") %>%
    group_by(grade) %>%
    arrange(desc(Percentile), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      cum_Under40   = cumsum(n_Under40),
      cum_40andOver = cumsum(n_40andOver),
      has_enough_data = Under40 >= min_n_threshold & `40andOver` >= min_n_threshold &
                        cum_Under40 >= min_n_threshold & cum_40andOver >= min_n_threshold,
      Under40_Avg_Theta                    = round(avg_th_Under40, 4),
      `40andOver_Avg_Theta`                = round(avg_th_40andOver, 4),
      `Theta_Diff_40andOver_minus_Under40` = round(avg_th_40andOver - avg_th_Under40, 4),
      Impact_Ratio_AIR                     = ifelse(
        has_enough_data,
        round((cum_40andOver / `40andOver`) / (cum_Under40 / Under40), 3),
        NA_real_
      ),
      Adverse_Impact_Flag = case_when(
        !has_enough_data        ~ "Insufficient Data",
        Impact_Ratio_AIR < 0.80 ~ "YES (AIR < 0.80)",
        TRUE                    ~ "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(grade, Percentile) %>%
    select(
      grade, Percentile,
      Under40_Count = n_Under40,
      `40andOver_Count` = n_40andOver,
      Under40_Avg_Theta,
      `40andOver_Avg_Theta`,
      `Theta_Diff_40andOver_minus_Under40`,
      Impact_Ratio_AIR,
      Adverse_Impact_Flag
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = grade,
      values_from = -c(grade, Percentile),
      names_glue = "{gsub(' ', '_', grade)}_{.value}"
    )
}

# 3. SUMMARIZE ADVERSE IMPACT ONSET PERCENTILE (Handling Insufficient Data without min() warnings)
summarize_ai_onset_age <- function(grid_df, model_label = "1PL Theta") {
  map_dfr(target_grades, \(g) {
    prefix   <- gsub(" ", "_", g)
    air_col  <- paste0(prefix, "_Impact_Ratio_AIR")
    flag_col <- paste0(prefix, "_Adverse_Impact_Flag")
    
    valid_rows <- grid_df %>% filter(.data[[flag_col]] != "Insufficient Data")
    ai_rows    <- valid_rows %>% filter(.data[[air_col]] < 0.80)
    insuff_pct <- grid_df %>% filter(.data[[flag_col]] == "Insufficient Data") %>% pull(Percentile)
    
    onset_text <- if (nrow(valid_rows) == 0) {
      "Insufficient Data"
    } else if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) {
      paste0("Starts at ", min(ai_rows$Percentile), "th percentile")
    } else {
      "No Adverse Impact"
    }
    
    tibble(
      Model             = model_label,
      Job_Grade         = g,
      AI_Onset_Pct      = onset_text,
      AIR_at_Onset      = if (nrow(ai_rows) > 0) ai_rows[[air_col]][which.min(ai_rows$Percentile)] else NA_real_,
      Min_Valid_AIR     = if (nrow(valid_rows) > 0) round(min(valid_rows[[air_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_,
      Insufficient_Pcts = if (length(insuff_pct) > 0) paste0(min(insuff_pct), "th–", max(insuff_pct), "th pct") else "None"
    )
  })
}
```

```{r}
# 2. VECTORIZED ADVERSE IMPACT GRID BUILDER (Strict < 5 Guardrail)
build_ai_grid_rel <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
  totals <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(grade, rel_grp, name = "total") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = rel_grp, values_from = total, values_fill = 0)
  
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    grade      = factor(target_grades, levels = target_grades),
    Percentile = 1:100,
    rel_grp    = c("Christian", "Other")
  ) %>%
    left_join(
      data %>%
        group_by(grade, Percentile = .data[[pct_col]], rel_grp) %>%
        summarise(n = n(), avg_th = mean(.data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("grade", "Percentile", "rel_grp")
    ) %>%
    mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = rel_grp, values_from = c(n, avg_th)) %>%
    left_join(totals, by = "grade") %>%
    mutate(
      Christian = replace_na(Christian, 0L),
      Other     = replace_na(Other, 0L)
    ) %>%
    group_by(grade) %>%
    arrange(desc(Percentile), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      cum_Christian = cumsum(n_Christian),
      cum_Other     = cumsum(n_Other),
      has_enough_data = !is.na(Christian) & !is.na(Other) &
                        Christian >= min_n_threshold & Other >= min_n_threshold &
                        n_Christian >= min_n_threshold & n_Other >= min_n_threshold &
                        cum_Christian >= min_n_threshold & cum_Other >= min_n_threshold,
      Christian_Avg_Theta              = ifelse(n_Christian >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_Christian, 4), NA_real_),
      Other_Avg_Theta                  = ifelse(n_Other >= min_n_threshold, round(avg_th_Other, 4), NA_real_),
      Theta_Diff_Other_minus_Christian = ifelse(
        n_Christian >= min_n_threshold & n_Other >= min_n_threshold,
        round(avg_th_Other - avg_th_Christian, 4),
        NA_real_
      ),
      Impact_Ratio_AIR                 = ifelse(
        has_enough_data,
        round((cum_Other / Other) / (cum_Christian / Christian), 3),
        NA_real_
      ),
      Adverse_Impact_Flag = case_when(
        !has_enough_data        ~ "Insufficient Data",
        Impact_Ratio_AIR < 0.80 ~ "YES (AIR < 0.80)",
        TRUE                    ~ "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(grade, Percentile) %>%
    select(
      grade, Percentile,
      Christian_Count = n_Christian,
      Other_Count     = n_Other,
      Christian_Avg_Theta,
      Other_Avg_Theta,
      Theta_Diff_Other_minus_Christian,
      Impact_Ratio_AIR,
      Adverse_Impact_Flag
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = grade,
      values_from = -c(grade, Percentile),
      names_glue  = "{gsub(' ', '_', grade)}_{.value}"
    )
}
```

## 7. Differential Item Functioning

DIF analysis contains summary of moderately and severely violating items and the direction f the violation. The analysis is based on the newly calculated Theta_1PL, which is IRT 1PL model.

Minimum number of 30 responses per group is used for the basis of DIF analysis for three reasons (GEMINI adapted);

-   ***Preventing Logistic Regression Breakdown:** Logistic regression relies on Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), which requires a minimum sample size to converge reliably.*

-   ***Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) Validity:** The `anova(mod0, mod1, test = "LRT")` test relies on an asymptotic* $\chi^2$ *approximation. Below* $N \approx 30$ *per group, that approximation degrades, making the resulting `p_val` unreliable.*

<!-- -->

-   ***Practical Balance for CAT Data:** Because Computerized Adaptive Testing distributes items unevenly, setting a strict cutoff too high can eliminate large portions of the item bank—especially for smaller focal groups (e.g., Sexual Orientation or Disability). A floor of 30 keeps the model mathematically stable while retaining as many items as possible.*

*In DIF literature (e.g., Swaminathan & Rogers, 1990; Zumbo, 1999; Scott et al., 2009), **100 to 200+ respondents per group** is typically recommended for strong statistical power to detect moderate DIF. At* $N = 30$*–*$50$*, the logistic regression will run cleanly and can catch severe DIF, but sampling noise will be higher—so, `N_Man`/`N_Woman` (and equivalent group counts) are included in the output tables to flag low-*$N$ *items during review.*

### 7.A Gender

(GEMINI) *LR-DIF conditions on the pre-computed Theta and tests if Gender predicts getting the item right using a standard `glm()`. **This is mathematically equivalent to the 1PL uniform DIF test**, returns the exact same effect sizes (wABC, ESSD, and log-odds shift), natively handles extreme CAT sparsity, and **runs instantly without hanging.***

```{r}
#| label: Gender-differential-item-functioning-1pl
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 0. ENSURE THETA IS AVAILABLE
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

# 1. EXTRACT & FILTER ALIGNED DATA
stopifnot(
  "mirt_active_matrix not found." = exists("mirt_active_matrix"),
  "scored_rows not found." = exists("scored_rows")
)

gender_col <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$gender[scored_rows]
gender_raw <- if (is.list(gender_col)) {
  vapply(gender_col, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
} else {
  as.character(gender_col)
}
gender_raw <- trimws(gender_raw)

valid_mask <- !is.na(gender_raw) & gender_raw %in% c("Man", "Woman")

dif_matrix <- as.matrix(mirt_active_matrix[valid_mask, , drop = FALSE])
dif_gender <- factor(gender_raw[valid_mask], levels = c("Man", "Woman"))
dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

cat("Sample sizes for Gender DIF:\n")
print(table(dif_gender))


# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)
min_n <- 30
keep_items <- sapply(colnames(dif_matrix), function(col) {
  x <- dif_matrix[, col]
  counts <- tapply(!is.na(x), dif_gender, sum)
  means  <- tapply(x, dif_gender, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (Woman) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting
woman_theta <- dif_theta[dif_gender == "Woman"]
woman_mean  <- mean(woman_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
woman_sd    <- sd(woman_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_grid  <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 61)
weights     <- dnorm(theta_grid, mean = woman_mean, sd = woman_sd)
weights     <- weights / sum(weights)

suppressWarnings({
  dif_results <- purrr::map_dfr(colnames(dif_matrix_clean), function(item_nm) {
    y    <- dif_matrix_clean[, item_nm]
    seen <- !is.na(y)
    
    df_item <- data.frame(
      score  = y[seen],
      theta  = dif_theta[seen],
      gender = dif_gender[seen]
    )
    
    # Model 0: Baseline 1PL (Score ~ Theta)
    mod0 <- glm(score ~ theta, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    # Model 1: Uniform DIF (Score ~ Theta + Gender)
    mod1 <- glm(score ~ theta + gender, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    
    # Likelihood Ratio Test
    lrt   <- anova(mod0, mod1, test = "LRT")
    p_val <- lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
    
    # Extract 1PL parameters from the GLM
    coefs  <- coef(mod1)
    a      <- coefs["theta"]
    d_man  <- coefs["(Intercept)"]
    d_diff <- if ("genderWoman" %in% names(coefs)) coefs["genderWoman"] else 0
    d_wom  <- d_man + d_diff
    
    # Calculate Exact Expected Score Curves
    p_man      <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_man)
    p_woman    <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_wom)
    diff_curve <- p_woman - p_man
    
    tibble(
      Item    = item_nm,
      N_Man   = sum(df_item$gender == "Man"),
      N_Woman = sum(df_item$gender == "Woman"),
      p_val   = p_val,
      d_Diff  = round(unname(d_diff), 4),
      wABC    = round(sum(abs(diff_curve) * weights), 4),
      ESSD    = round(sum(diff_curve * weights), 4)
    )
  })
})


# 4. ADJUST P-VALUES AND SUMMARIZE
dif_results <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    adj_pvals = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
    Favors = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "No Significant DIF",
      ESSD > 0          ~ "Woman (Focal)",
      ESSD < 0          ~ "Man (Reference)",
      TRUE              ~ "Neutral"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(adj_pvals)

# View all statistically significant DIF items (BH-adjusted p < 0.05)
flagged_gender_dif <- dif_results %>%
  filter(adj_pvals < 0.05) %>%
  select(Item, N_Man, N_Woman, p_val, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, ESSD, Favors)

print(flagged_gender_dif)

# 5. DIF SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION & SUMMARY REPORT
dif_summary <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    DIF_Severity = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "Not Significant",
      wABC >= 0.20      ~ "Severe",
      wABC >= 0.10      ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE              ~ "Negligible"
    )
  )

# 5a. Print High-Level Summary Counts
severity_counts <- dif_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(DIF_Severity, name = "Item_Count") %>%
  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))

cat("\n=== GENDER DIF OVERALL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(knitr::kable(severity_counts))

# 5b. Extract and Print Actionable Items (Moderate or Severe)
actionable_items <- dif_summary %>%
  filter(DIF_Severity %in% c("Moderate", "Severe")) %>%
  arrange(desc(wABC)) %>%
  select(Item, DIF_Severity, N_Man, N_Woman, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, Favors)

cat("\n=== MODERATE & SEVERE ITEMS REQUIRING REVIEW ===\n")
if (nrow(actionable_items) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(actionable_items))
} else {
  cat("No items exhibited Moderate or Severe Gender DIF. Any statistically significant items have negligible effect sizes.\n")
}
```

> *INTERPRETATION: (GEMINI) If `adj_pvals < 0.05`, the item exhibits statistically significant Differential Item Functioning (DIF). The Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment prevents false positives that happen when testing dozens or hundreds of items simultaneously.*
>
> -   ***Caveat:** In large datasets, even microscopic, meaningless differences will flag as statistically significant. That is why you must look at `wABC` next.*
>
> ***`wABC` (Weighted Area Between Curves — Effect Size)** This measures the practical magnitude of the bias. It calculates the physical space between the Men's and Women's probability curves, heavily weighted toward where the majority of the Focal group (Women) actually scores.*
>
> -   ***\< 0.10:** Negligible DIF. The item is statistically flagged, but the bias is too tiny to meaningfully impact scores. Usually safe to keep.*
>
> -   ***0.10 to 0.20:** Moderate DIF. The item shows noticeable bias. Review the item's content for obvious stereotyping or biased language.*
>
> -   ***\> 0.20:** Severe DIF. The item functions completely differently for men and women. It should typically be removed from the scoring model and the item bank.*
>
> -   ***`d_Diff` (Log-Odds Difficulty Shift)** This tells you the direction and raw size of the mathematical shift in the logistic regression.*
>
>     -   ***Positive value:** The item is easier for the Focal group (Women) compared to Men of the same ability.*
>
>     -   ***Negative value:** The item is easier for the Reference group (Men) compared to Women of the same ability.*
>
>     ***`N_Man` and `N_Woman`** Because this is Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT), not everyone saw every item. These columns confirm exactly how many men and women were administered this specific question. If an item flags for severe DIF but only has 32 men and 35 women, the effect size might be unstable noise rather than a structural flaw in the question.*

### 7.B Disability

```{r}
#| label: Disability-differential-item-functioning-1pl
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 0. ENSURE THETA IS AVAILABLE
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

# 1. EXTRACT & FILTER ALIGNED DATA
stopifnot(
  "mirt_active_matrix not found." = exists("mirt_active_matrix"),
  "scored_rows not found." = exists("scored_rows")
)

# Identify the disability column (handles potential naming variations)
disab_col_name <- intersect(
  c("disability", "do_you_have_a_disability", "disability.x", "disability.y"), 
  colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)
)[1]
if (is.na(disab_col_name)) disab_col_name <- "disability"

disab_col <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[disab_col_name]][scored_rows]

# Safely flatten list-columns
disab_raw <- if (is.list(disab_col)) {
  vapply(disab_col, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
} else {
  as.character(disab_col)
}
disab_raw <- trimws(disab_raw)

# Keep only rows explicitly coded as 'No' or 'Yes'
valid_mask <- !is.na(disab_raw) & disab_raw %in% c("No", "Yes")

dif_matrix <- as.matrix(mirt_active_matrix[valid_mask, , drop = FALSE])
# Set 'No' as Reference group (level 1) and 'Yes' as Focal group (level 2)
dif_disab  <- factor(disab_raw[valid_mask], levels = c("No", "Yes"))
dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

cat("Sample sizes for Disability DIF:\n")
print(table(dif_disab))


# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)
min_n <- 30
keep_items <- sapply(colnames(dif_matrix), function(col) {
  x <- dif_matrix[, col]
  counts <- tapply(!is.na(x), dif_disab, sum)
  means  <- tapply(x, dif_disab, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (Yes) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting
yes_theta  <- dif_theta[dif_disab == "Yes"]
yes_mean   <- mean(yes_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
yes_sd     <- sd(yes_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_grid <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 61)
weights    <- dnorm(theta_grid, mean = yes_mean, sd = yes_sd)
weights    <- weights / sum(weights)

suppressWarnings({
  dif_results <- purrr::map_dfr(colnames(dif_matrix_clean), function(item_nm) {
    y    <- dif_matrix_clean[, item_nm]
    seen <- !is.na(y)
    
    df_item <- data.frame(
      score  = y[seen],
      theta  = dif_theta[seen],
      disab  = dif_disab[seen]
    )
    
    # Model 0: Baseline 1PL (Score ~ Theta)
    mod0 <- glm(score ~ theta, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    # Model 1: Uniform DIF (Score ~ Theta + Disability)
    mod1 <- glm(score ~ theta + disab, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    
    # Likelihood Ratio Test
    lrt   <- anova(mod0, mod1, test = "LRT")
    p_val <- lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
    
    # Extract 1PL parameters from the GLM
    coefs  <- coef(mod1)
    a      <- coefs["theta"]
    d_no   <- coefs["(Intercept)"]
    d_diff <- if ("disabYes" %in% names(coefs)) coefs["disabYes"] else 0
    d_yes  <- d_no + d_diff
    
    # Calculate Exact Expected Score Curves
    p_no       <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_no)
    p_yes      <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_yes)
    diff_curve <- p_yes - p_no
    
    tibble(
      Item    = item_nm,
      N_No    = sum(df_item$disab == "No"),
      N_Yes   = sum(df_item$disab == "Yes"),
      p_val   = p_val,
      d_Diff  = round(unname(d_diff), 4),
      wABC    = round(sum(abs(diff_curve) * weights), 4),
      ESSD    = round(sum(diff_curve * weights), 4)
    )
  })
})


# 4. ADJUST P-VALUES AND SUMMARIZE
dif_results <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    adj_pvals = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
    Favors = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "No Significant DIF",
      ESSD > 0          ~ "Yes (Focal)",
      ESSD < 0          ~ "No (Reference)",
      TRUE              ~ "Neutral"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(adj_pvals)

# View all statistically significant DIF items (BH-adjusted p < 0.05)
flagged_disab_dif <- dif_results %>%
  filter(adj_pvals < 0.05) %>%
  select(Item, N_No, N_Yes, p_val, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, ESSD, Favors)

print(flagged_disab_dif)


# 5. DIF SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION & SUMMARY REPORT
dif_summary <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    DIF_Severity = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "Not Significant",
      wABC >= 0.20      ~ "Severe",
      wABC >= 0.10      ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE              ~ "Negligible"
    )
  )

# 5a. Print High-Level Summary Counts
severity_counts <- dif_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(DIF_Severity, name = "Item_Count") %>%
  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))

cat("\n=== DISABILITY DIF OVERALL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(knitr::kable(severity_counts))

# 5b. Extract and Print Actionable Items (Moderate or Severe)
actionable_items <- dif_summary %>%
  filter(DIF_Severity %in% c("Moderate", "Severe")) %>%
  arrange(desc(wABC)) %>%
  select(Item, DIF_Severity, N_No, N_Yes, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, Favors)

cat("\n=== MODERATE & SEVERE ITEMS REQUIRING REVIEW ===\n")
if (nrow(actionable_items) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(actionable_items))
} else {
  cat("No items exhibited Moderate or Severe Disability DIF. Any statistically significant items have negligible effect sizes.\n")
}
```

```{r}
)

  "Asian / Asian British",

  "Other ethnic group"
)

# Identify the ethnicity column

} else {
  as.character(eth_col)
}
eth_raw <- trimws(eth_raw)

# Map to Reference ("White") vs Focal ("Others")
eth_grp <- case_when(
  str_detect(eth_raw, "(?i)^white") ~ "White",
  eth_raw %in% focal_ethnicities | str_detect(eth_raw, "(?i)^(asian|black|mixed|other ethnic)") ~ "Others",

)

# Keep only rows mapped to 'White' or 'Others'

dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)

  x <- dif_matrix[, col]
  counts <- tapply(!is.na(x), dif_eth, sum)
  means  <- tapply(x, dif_eth, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (Others) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting
others_theta <- dif_theta[dif_eth == "Others"]
others_mean  <- mean(others_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
others_sd    <- sd(others_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_grid   <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 61)
weights      <- dnorm(theta_grid, mean = others_mean, sd = others_sd)
weights      <- weights / sum(weights)

suppressWarnings({
  dif_results <- purrr::map_dfr(colnames(dif_matrix_clean), function(item_nm) {
    y    <- dif_matrix_clean[, item_nm]
    seen <- !is.na(y)
    
    df_item <- data.frame(
      score = y[seen],
      theta = dif_theta[seen],
      eth   = dif_eth[seen]
    )
    
    # Model 0: Baseline 1PL (Score ~ Theta)
    mod0 <- glm(score ~ theta, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    # Model 1: Uniform DIF (Score ~ Theta + Ethnicity)
    mod1 <- glm(score ~ theta + eth, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    
    # Likelihood Ratio Test
    lrt   <- anova(mod0, mod1, test = "LRT")
    p_val <- lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]

    coefs    <- coef(mod1)
    a        <- coefs["theta"]

    d_diff   <- if ("ethOthers" %in% names(coefs)) coefs["ethOthers"] else 0
    d_others <- d_white + d_diff
    
    # Calculate Exact Expected Score Curves
    p_white    <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_white)
    p_others   <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_others)
    diff_curve <- p_others - p_white
    
    tibble(
      Item     = item_nm,
      N_White  = sum(df_item$eth == "White"),
      N_Others = sum(df_item$eth == "Others"),
      p_val    = p_val,
      d_Diff   = round(unname(d_diff), 4),
      wABC     = round(sum(abs(diff_curve) * weights), 4),
      ESSD     = round(sum(diff_curve * weights), 4)
    )
  })
})


# 4. ADJUST P-VALUES AND SUMMARIZE

    )

  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))
```

```{r}
    )
  )

# 5a. Print High-Level Summary Counts
severity_counts <- dif_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(DIF_Severity, name = "Item_Count") %>%
  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))

cat("\n=== SEXUAL ORIENTATION DIF OVERALL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(knitr::kable(severity_counts))

# 5b. Extract and Print Actionable Items (Moderate or Severe)
actionable_items <- dif_summary %>%
  filter(DIF_Severity %in% c("Moderate", "Severe")) %>%
  arrange(desc(wABC)) %>%
  select(Item, DIF_Severity, N_Het, N_Other, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, Favors)

cat("\n=== MODERATE & SEVERE ITEMS REQUIRING REVIEW ===\n")
if (nrow(actionable_items) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(actionable_items))
} else {
  cat("No items exhibited Moderate or Severe Sexual Orientation DIF. Any statistically significant items have negligible effect sizes.\n")
```

### 7.E Age

```{r}
#| label: Age-differential-item-functioning-1pl
#| message: false
#| warning: false


# 0. ENSURE THETA IS AVAILABLE
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {
  CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
}

# 1. EXTRACT & FILTER ALIGNED DATA
stopifnot(
  "mirt_active_matrix not found." = exists("mirt_active_matrix"),
  "scored_rows not found." = exists("scored_rows")
)

# Identify the age column
age_col_name <- intersect(
  c("select_your_current_age_group", "select_your_current_age_group.y", "select_your_current_age_group.x"), 
  colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)
)[1]
stopifnot(!is.na(age_col_name))

age_col <- CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025[[age_col_name]][scored_rows]

# Safely flatten list-columns
age_raw <- if (is.list(age_col)) {
  vapply(age_col, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
} else {
  as.character(age_col)
}
age_raw <- trimws(age_raw)

# Map to Reference ("Under40") vs Focal ("40andOver")
age_grp <- case_when(
  str_detect(age_raw, "^(16-24|25-29|30-34|35-39)$")             ~ "Under40",
  str_detect(age_raw, "^(40-44|45-49|50-54|55-59|60-64|65\\+)$") ~ "40andOver",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

# Keep only rows mapped to 'Under40' or '40andOver'
valid_mask <- !is.na(age_grp) & age_grp %in% c("Under40", "40andOver")

dif_matrix <- as.matrix(mirt_active_matrix[valid_mask, , drop = FALSE])
# Set 'Under40' as Reference group (level 1) and '40andOver' as Focal group (level 2)
dif_age    <- factor(age_grp[valid_mask], levels = c("Under40", "40andOver"))
dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

cat("Sample sizes for Age DIF:\n")
print(table(dif_age))


# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)
min_n <- 30
keep_items <- sapply(colnames(dif_matrix), function(col) {
  x <- dif_matrix[, col]
  counts <- tapply(!is.na(x), dif_age, sum)
  means  <- tapply(x, dif_age, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (40andOver) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting
over40_theta <- dif_theta[dif_age == "40andOver"]
over40_mean  <- mean(over40_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
over40_sd    <- sd(over40_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_grid   <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 61)
weights      <- dnorm(theta_grid, mean = over40_mean, sd = over40_sd)
weights      <- weights / sum(weights)

suppressWarnings({
  dif_results <- purrr::map_dfr(colnames(dif_matrix_clean), function(item_nm) {
    y    <- dif_matrix_clean[, item_nm]
    seen <- !is.na(y)
    
    df_item <- data.frame(
      score = y[seen],
      theta = dif_theta[seen],
      age   = dif_age[seen]
    )
    
    # Model 0: Baseline 1PL (Score ~ Theta)
    mod0 <- glm(score ~ theta, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    # Model 1: Uniform DIF (Score ~ Theta + Age Group)
    mod1 <- glm(score ~ theta + age, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    
    # Likelihood Ratio Test
    lrt   <- anova(mod0, mod1, test = "LRT")
    p_val <- lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
    
    # Extract 1PL parameters from the GLM
    coefs    <- coef(mod1)
    a        <- coefs["theta"]
    d_under  <- coefs["(Intercept)"]
    d_diff   <- if ("age40andOver" %in% names(coefs)) coefs["age40andOver"] else 0
    d_over   <- d_under + d_diff
    
    # Calculate Exact Expected Score Curves
    p_under    <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_under)
    p_over     <- plogis(a * theta_grid + d_over)
    diff_curve <- p_over - p_under
    
    tibble(
      Item        = item_nm,
      N_Under40   = sum(df_item$age == "Under40"),
      N_40andOver = sum(df_item$age == "40andOver"),
      p_val       = p_val,
      d_Diff      = round(unname(d_diff), 4),
      wABC        = round(sum(abs(diff_curve) * weights), 4),
      ESSD        = round(sum(diff_curve * weights), 4)
    )
  })
})


# 4. ADJUST P-VALUES AND SUMMARIZE
dif_results <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    adj_pvals = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
    Favors = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "No Significant DIF",
      ESSD > 0          ~ "40 and Over (Focal)",
      ESSD < 0          ~ "Under 40 (Reference)",
      TRUE              ~ "Neutral"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(adj_pvals)

# View all statistically significant DIF items (BH-adjusted p < 0.05)
flagged_age_dif <- dif_results %>%
  filter(adj_pvals < 0.05) %>%
  select(Item, N_Under40, N_40andOver, p_val, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, ESSD, Favors)

print(flagged_age_dif)


# 5. DIF SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION & SUMMARY REPORT
dif_summary <- dif_results %>%
  mutate(
    DIF_Severity = case_when(
      adj_pvals >= 0.05 ~ "Not Significant",
      wABC >= 0.20      ~ "Severe",
      wABC >= 0.10      ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE              ~ "Negligible"
    )
  )

# 5a. Print High-Level Summary Counts
severity_counts <- dif_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(DIF_Severity, name = "Item_Count") %>%
  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))

cat("\n=== AGE DIF OVERALL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(knitr::kable(severity_counts))

# 5b. Extract and Print Actionable Items (Moderate or Severe)
actionable_items <- dif_summary %>%
  filter(DIF_Severity %in% c("Moderate", "Severe")) %>%
  arrange(desc(wABC)) %>%
  select(Item, DIF_Severity, N_Under40, N_40andOver, adj_pvals, d_Diff, wABC, Favors)

cat("\n=== MODERATE & SEVERE ITEMS REQUIRING REVIEW ===\n")
if (nrow(actionable_items) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(actionable_items))
} else {
  cat("No items exhibited Moderate or Severe Age DIF. Any statistically significant items have negligible effect sizes.\n")
}
```

### 7.F Religion

```{r}
#| label: Religion-differential-item-functioning-1pl

# 0. ENSURE THETA IS AVAILABLE
if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)) {

}

# 1. EXTRACT & FILTER ALIGNED DATA

  "mirt_active_matrix not found." = exists("mirt_active_matrix"),
  "scored_rows not found." = exists("scored_rows")
)

focal_religions <- c("No religion", "Muslim", "Hindu", "Sikh", "Other religion", "Buddhist", "Jewish")

# Identify the religion column
rel_col_name <- intersect(
  c("what_is_your_religion_or_belief", "what_is_your_religion_or_belief.y", "what_is_your_religion_or_belief.x"), 
  colnames(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025)
)[1]

# Safely flatten list-columns

  vapply(rel_col, \(v) if (length(v) == 0 || all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else as.character(v[[1]]), character(1))
} else {
  as.character(rel_col)
}
rel_raw <- trimws(rel_raw)

# Map to Reference ("Christian") vs Focal ("Other")
rel_grp <- case_when(
  str_detect(rel_raw, "(?i)^christian$") ~ "Christian",
  rel_raw %in% focal_religions | 
    str_detect(rel_raw, "(?i)^(no religion|muslim|hindu|sikh|other religion|buddhist|jewish)$") ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

# Keep only rows mapped to 'Christian' or 'Other'
valid_mask <- !is.na(rel_grp) & rel_grp %in% c("Christian", "Other")

dif_matrix <- as.matrix(mirt_active_matrix[valid_mask, , drop = FALSE])
# Set 'Christian' as Reference group (level 1) and 'Other' as Focal group (level 2)
dif_rel    <- factor(rel_grp[valid_mask], levels = c("Christian", "Other"))
dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)

  counts <- tapply(!is.na(x), dif_rel, sum)
  means  <- tapply(x, dif_rel, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (Other) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting
other_theta <- dif_theta[dif_rel == "Other"]
other_mean  <- mean(other_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
other_sd    <- sd(other_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_grid  <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 61)
weights     <- dnorm(theta_grid, mean = other_mean, sd = other_sd)
weights     <- weights / sum(weights)

suppressWarnings({
  dif_results <- purrr::map_dfr(colnames(dif_matrix_clean), function(item_nm) {
    y    <- dif_matrix_clean[, item_nm]
    seen <- !is.na(y)
    
    df_item <- data.frame(
      score = y[seen],
      theta = dif_theta[seen],
      rel   = dif_rel[seen]
    )
    
    # Model 0: Baseline 1PL (Score ~ Theta)
    mod0 <- glm(score ~ theta, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    # Model 1: Uniform DIF (Score ~ Theta + Religion)
    mod1 <- glm(score ~ theta + rel, data = df_item, family = binomial)
    
    # Likelihood Ratio Test

    )

} else {
```

```{r}
}
ses_raw <- trimws(ses_raw)

# Map to Reference ("Lower_SES") vs Focal ("Higher_SES") based on leading text

  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

# Keep only rows mapped to 'Lower_SES' or 'Higher_SES'

dif_matrix <- as.matrix(mirt_active_matrix[valid_mask, , drop = FALSE])
# Set 'Lower_SES' as Reference group (level 1) and 'Higher_SES' as Focal group (level 2)

dif_theta  <- as.numeric(CSNT_Item_Diversity_Scored_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_rows][valid_mask])

# 2. FILTER SPARSE ITEMS (Min 30 per group, strictly varying)

  means  <- tapply(x, dif_ses, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  all(!is.na(counts)) && all(counts >= min_n) &&
    all(!is.na(means)) && all(means > 0 & means < 1)
})

dif_matrix_clean <- dif_matrix[, keep_items, drop = FALSE]
cat("Items retained for DIF:", ncol(dif_matrix_clean), "of", ncol(dif_matrix), "\n")


# 3. RUN LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIF (INSTANT & NON-HANGING)
# Define focal group (Higher_SES) latent distribution for Expected Score weighting

higher_mean  <- mean(higher_theta, na.rm = TRUE)
higher_sd    <- sd(higher_theta, na.rm = TRUE)

suppressWarnings({

      ESSD > 0          ~ "Higher SES (Focal)",

    )
  )

# 5a. Print High-Level Summary Counts

  dplyr::count(DIF_Severity, name = "Item_Count") %>%
  arrange(match(DIF_Severity, c("Severe", "Moderate", "Negligible", "Not Significant")))

cat("\n=== SES DIF OVERALL SUMMARY ===\n")

cat("\n=== MODERATE & SEVERE ITEMS REQUIRING REVIEW ===\n")
```
